about: What DAStastic does in the current build, area by area: the Current build section of static/release-notes.html is rendered from this file by tools/build_features.py. Each feature traces to a release (its id in src) or a file. A release with New or Improved lines must be in some feature's src (tests/test_release_notes.py).

areas.name: Start
areas.summary: One DAS job taken step by step from an address to the AHJ package, in plain questions for someone with no RF background.

features.name: Four steps, one job
features.text: Start takes one job through Discovery, Survey, Design and AHJ package with plain questions and drop-downs. A Start job is an ordinary DAS job, so the DAS tab shows the same record.

features.name: Start takes what you have
features.text: Every box on the building form can stay blank and the Discovery report still builds. The report lists what was left blank, and Fill them in goes back to the form.

features.name: Discovery report
features.text: One page from an address and a few answers: whether a system is likely needed, the likely AHJ, systems and bands in play, radio shops' FCC contacts, each carrier's coverage, nearest site and bands, and what takes a phone call. Prints as PDF.

features.name: Main system named
features.text: The report marks the main radio system: the strongest in the top tier, preferring an agency named for the building's town or county. Those systems are ticked on the job's Pre-survey, except on a cellular job.

features.name: Report without the outline wait
features.text: The Discovery report runs without waiting on the building outline, which takes up to 43 seconds on a first visit. The outline is fetched in the background for Plans and the Overview.

features.name: The law and the AHJ's say
features.text: Under the estimate, the report says what the state's law reads for this building and who at the AHJ confirmed it, with Open the Code check a press away. It says the AHJ has final authority and its written word wins.

features.name: You pick the AHJ
features.text: The report lists the three most likely fire departments with phone and reason. This one sets the job's AHJ and its contact; nothing is picked for you.

features.name: Rough pin for unlisted buildings
features.text: An address on no list yet, most often a building under construction, goes on the map at its street, ZIP or town. The address stays as typed, and the report says the pin is rough until someone moves it.

features.name: The proper address saved
features.text: A pick from the address list stays picked. An address nobody picked saves as the best match's full address with state and ZIP, and only when the house number matches.

features.name: Next always goes on
features.text: Next and the step strip never wait on a blank answer. A step stays unticked until the job's record shows it done, and what's still open is said on the step and its summary.

features.name: Start moves the stage
features.text: Moving on to Survey, Design or Install moves the job's stage through the DAS tab's own gate. Each step lists ahead what the file is missing, with Open and a plain hint for each, and moving on anyway takes a reason.

features.name: Skip with a reason
features.text: Any step can be skipped with a reason. The skip stays on the job, prints on the report and the design submittal, and can be taken back.

features.name: Walk the building
features.text: Survey asks yes or no about getting in, the head-end room, the path between floors, the roof and photos; a No asks for the plan. The summary prints or saves.

features.name: Grid test guidance
features.text: Survey explains how to run the grid test and counts the squares measured. Readings with no calibrated instrument on the job say they don't count, and why.

features.name: When a grid test fails
features.text: A failed floor brings ten things to check ahead of the retest, in the order a technician would. Walk it in the fault chart opens the fault chart at that fault.

features.name: Design checklist
features.text: Design lists what the job needs: floor plans, bands and antennas, a started parts list, a part number and price on every line, and licensee consent asked on public safety jobs. Each line opens its DAS tab and ticks itself.

features.name: AHJ package step
features.text: The AHJ's own list is checked against the job, with what's missing named. It opens the Report to print or seal, downloads the parts list and spec sheets, records the delivery date, and moves the job to Install once the AHJ approves.

features.name: Cellular jobs from Start
features.text: Start's answer on what the job covers decides public safety, cellular or both. A cellular job ticks no public safety agencies and fetches the area's cell sites for the report.

features.name: Carry on with a job
features.text: Start lists the jobs begun there with the step each is on. Open in the full tool shows the job on the DAS tab, and Back to Start returns to the step it left.

features.name: Open DAStastic on Start
features.text: A box at the foot of Start makes DAStastic open on Start instead of the Map, in this browser.

features.name: Guides and files from Start
features.text: A job on Start has buttons for Walk me through and for dropping files already in hand, and shows the job's Emails this job needs list under each step.

areas.name: Map
areas.summary: Every result around the pin as dots on a map, with the search line above it, a list or table below, and each emitter's details, coverage and network.

features.name: One line over the map
features.text: Where, how far, who and what frequency sit on one line above the map with Fixed sites only and Search, on every tab but Start. On a phone the map comes first, with its tools under it.

features.name: Pin, county or nationwide
features.text: The pin box takes an address, place, county, coordinates or a Maps link, or a click, drag or GPS; radius 0.25 to 50 miles. A county searches the whole county; Nationwide searches licences anywhere by call sign, licensee, service, technology or frequency.

features.name: What a search loads
features.text: One search loads every layer inside the circle or county, nearest first: FCC licences, expired or removed licences, towers, broadcast, NOAA Weather Radio, FAA aviation, 911 centres, earth stations, your captures and imported layers, each with distance and bearing from the pin.

features.name: Crowd and network layers
features.text: OpenCelliD cells, LoRaWAN gateways, SatNOGS stations, PSKReporter monitors, Meshtastic mesh radios and Helium hotspots load with the search where they're kept. WiGLE, RepeaterBook and WSPR show in the personal build only.

features.name: Towers follow the filters
features.text: With a frequency or text filter on, towers show only when they carry a matching licence or their owner matches.

features.name: Searches run by themselves
features.text: On a desktop, a change to the text, frequency, Fixed sites only or FCC fields searches after a short pause. On a phone it waits for the button, which says Search to apply.

features.name: A frequency box that reads RF
features.text: One box takes a channel (852.3625), a range (851-869), a tolerance (852.3625 ±12.5k), a band (B13, n77, VHF, NPSPAC) or a pasted list. A single number means that channel; a land mobile uplink brings its paired downlink.

features.name: Band picker
features.text: Beside the frequency box, a picker lists land mobile and cellular bands by their RF names, with Down, Up or Both for a paired band.

features.name: FCC licence search fields
features.text: FCC fields fold open under the search line: presets for aviation, public safety, business, marine, paging and broadcast auxiliary, radio service codes with names, technology, emission, grant and expiry dates, and From and To MHz.

features.name: Every source follows the search
features.text: Text and frequency filter every source, 911 centres, earth stations and crowd rows included. Rows that list no frequency are left off a frequency search and counted, Show them brings them back, and an empty range says why.

features.name: What's filtered, in words
features.text: Over the map a line reads like 376 of 468 within 5 mi, fixed sites, then a pill per filter, search text and frequency included. A pill clears its own filter; Clear all clears everything, with Undo.

features.name: Saved views
features.text: Views over the map: Public safety discovery, Cellular discovery, Donor search, Interference hunt and Prospect area, plus your own named views kept in this browser. A view keeps the pin you're on.

features.name: Dots, pop-ups, list and table
features.text: One dot per site, coloured by signal type. Its pop-up lists up to 14 entries with coverage, network, cell site and measured links; beside the map, a list under distance headings or a sortable table.

features.name: The pin and pin lock
features.text: Drag the pin or click the map to move it and search again. Lock it and clicks select dots instead, the pin lets clicks through, and the choice is kept in this browser.

features.name: Rings, scale and readout
features.text: Labelled distance rings at a round step and the radius ring, a miles and kilometres scale bar, and a readout of the cursor's position, distance and bearing from the pin.

features.name: Wheel-zoom lock
features.text: Every map opens with mouse-wheel zoom locked, so the wheel scrolls the page; hold the left button or Ctrl and scroll to zoom. The lock button frees the wheel until DAStastic is opened again. Zoom bar top right, layers top left.

features.name: Base maps
features.text: Street (OpenStreetMap), Satellite and Satellite + labels (USGS), Satellite hi-res (Esri), Topo and Terrain relief (USGS), remembered. With no signal, a street or Esri map shows USGS Topo and comes back when signal does.

features.name: Map overlays
features.text: County and state lines, microwave backhaul from zoom 8 (pending filings dashed), and live NEXRAD weather radar. Live ships (AIS) are in the personal build only.

features.name: Boundaries
features.text: State, county and city / town lines from the Census Bureau's 1:500,000 boundary files (2025), each switched on alone or All boundaries for the three, in every map's layers and in DAStastic lite's Layers and filters. They draw under every other layer and never take a click; counties load for the states in view from zoom 7, cities and towns from zoom 9, state and county names where they fit, city and town names on the satellite and relief maps. The web version and lite keep the ones seen for use with no signal.

features.name: Map styles
features.text: Standard, ATAK style (2525-style frames, imagery, MGRS in the readout), or your own map: an ATAK or WinTAK map source, a tile address or an MBTiles file.

features.name: Heatmaps
features.text: Predicted with terrain (Hata and hills, strongest 60), predicted free-space, measured from captures and crowd layers by file or signal, FCC carrier coverage by carrier, technology and setting, or density. They follow the filters, with an opacity slider.

features.name: Heatmap export
features.text: Heatmap (KMZ + GeoTIFF) downloads the heatmap as a KMZ for Google Earth and ATAK and a GeoTIFF for QGIS, ArcGIS or Global Mapper.

features.name: On this spot
features.text: Click a dot and the panel under the map lists everything at that spot, lit up in the table, with Coverage, Network, Cell site and Details for each.

features.name: Emitter coverage
features.text: Where one emitter reaches, by Hata or free space with terrain, antenna pattern and settings you change: a heatmap, the edge, reach each way, the level and path profile to the pin. Exports KMZ or ATAK.

features.name: Emitter network
features.text: A licence's base stations, mobiles and radio count, channel pairs, simulcast, other call signs and licences, others on its channels, its tower and co-tenants, microwave links, your labels and imported talk groups. Fit it on the map.

features.name: Details window
features.text: Details opens from a pop-up, a list double-click or any table row: source, signal type, how identified, distance and bearing; for a licence its call sign with FCC link, status, service, station type, decoded emissions, power, antenna, height and tower.

features.name: Band and channel for every signal
features.text: Details gives any signal's US band, wavelength, channel under each plan that covers it (FM, TV, NOAA, MURS, FRS and GMRS, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth LE, LTE, 5G, GNSS, ADS-B, AIS), the frequency it pairs with, what a scan adds and every field on file.

features.name: Merged sources
features.text: The same emitter from several sources shows once, the most trusted leading. Details lists who reported it, how many independent origins, a single source badge, and each source's value where they disagree.

features.name: Labels and on-site marks
features.text: Details saves your alpha tag, tone, NAC or colour code, tag, description, notes and Verified in use on a licence. With a mission active it also saves heard or not heard, a level and notes.

features.name: Tower details
features.text: A tower's Details show its registration, type, heights, owner, status and the licences on it. A carrier-owned tower reads as that carrier's registered structure: the owner on the FCC record, not proof of who's on it.

features.name: RadioReference links
features.text: Every licence in Details links to its call sign on RadioReference and to RadioReference's page of that state's systems and counties.

features.name: Radio ID look-up
features.text: A DMR or NXDN reading with a radio ID gets Who is it?: call sign, name and place from RadioID.net, one look-up at a time, each answer kept 30 days.

features.name: Signal ID Wiki matches
features.text: Details lists what a frequency could be from the Signal Identification Wiki, linked to each page. Personal build only: Cody's PC and the server's admin login; team logins, the sold build and the web version leave it out.

features.name: Artemis waterfalls and audio
features.text: In the personal build, with the Artemis library switched on in Data & updates, each Signal ID Wiki match shows its waterfall and plays its audio.

areas.name: Search
areas.summary: One box over everything DAStastic holds, opened from any tab with Ctrl+K.

features.name: Search everything
features.text: One box searches places, licences by call sign, licensee or frequency, towers and ASR numbers, 911 centres, broadcast, aviation, NOAA, microwave links, labels, talk groups, survey and crowd points, missions, FCC equipment makers, DAS jobs, contacts, files and the DAS research.

features.name: Ctrl+K from anywhere
features.text: Ctrl+K (or ⌘K) opens Search from any tab. Results come as you type, after a short pause, or at once on Enter.

features.name: Grouped, nearest first
features.text: Results come grouped by kind with a count per group that jumps to it, nearest to the pin first, with the matching words marked and the time the search took.

features.name: Narrow by kind
features.text: Buttons narrow the search to Places, Licences & frequencies, Towers, 911 centres, Broadcast, aviation, NOAA, Microwave, Surveys & crowd, Missions, or DAS & research.

features.name: Town plus kind
features.text: 'Charlotte fire' reads as a town and a kind of licensee and lists the licences around that town, one row per licensee, with the shared city and county systems after the fire ones.

features.name: Go from a result
features.text: Each result has its way there: the map with the emitter picked, its network or coverage, a talk group's system, a maker's FCC IDs, the mission, the DAS job at the field that matched, contacts, or the file.

features.name: Names while indexing
features.text: Licensee names come from an index rebuilt once after each FCC update, about a minute. Until it's ready Search says so, finds call signs and frequencies, and asks again by itself.

areas.name: Area report
areas.summary: Everything licensed around the pin on one page, and how far to trust each survey and crowd finding there.

features.name: Summary and tiles
features.text: One sentence sums up the area: licensed frequencies, licensees, bands, share digital, towers and the nearest licensed site, and says when filters shape the counts. Tiles jump to their section.

features.name: Bands table
features.text: Each band's range, frequencies, licensees, mix of technologies, nearest site and strongest estimated level, with a Coverage button that draws that band.

features.name: Coverage by band
features.text: A map of one band's predicted coverage from licensed power with Hata and the hills, for a handheld at 1.5 m, clear where it falls below the level you pick (−100 to −20 dBm).

features.name: Technologies and every frequency
features.text: A technologies table with frequencies, licensees and bands for each, then every licensed frequency by band with licensee, call sign, emission, ERP, distance and estimated level, 60 per band.

features.name: Unlisted signals
features.text: Every capture and crowd point is checked against FCC licences on its frequency within 40 miles, then bands that allow transmitting without a site licence. What's left is Unlisted: listed first, red on the map.

features.name: What an unlisted signal could be
features.text: In the personal build, each Unlisted finding also names up to three things the Signal Identification Wiki says it could be, each linked to its page.

features.name: How far to trust it
features.text: Each finding gets a grade in words (Confirmed, Probably true, Possibly true, Doubtful, Improbable, Can't judge), its source's letter A to F and a one-line why. Confirmed takes two independent origins agreeing on something diagnostic, one of them your capture.

features.name: Single source and old rows
features.text: A finding only one origin backs carries a single source badge, and copies of one source count once: ten copies of a crowd report are one source. Rows past their refresh age fade.

features.name: Warning flags
features.text: A reading louder than its licence allows at that distance, a decoded call sign that isn't the licence's, and a bearing more than 20° off the licensed site are each flagged.

features.name: Licensed, not heard
features.text: Where captures swept a band, it lists FCC licences loud enough there that the sweep would have heard them, with nothing on their frequency. A few spot readings don't count as a sweep.

features.name: Carrier coverage vs captures
features.text: Where a capture decoded cell IDs, it sets each carrier's FCC Broadband Map claim against what was heard: Claimed, not heard, and Weaker than claimed, more than 10 dB under the map. The map is modelled outdoors.

features.name: Track record
features.text: Pooled across every mission, it counts how often each source's claims held up against your captures. After 20 outcomes a source earns its own grade, marked ✓, in place of the proposed one.

features.name: Print and notices
features.text: The report prints, shows the date of the FCC data, carries the FCC's and OpenCelliD's notices, and links to RadioReference's state page to compare with what scanner listeners logged.

areas.name: Analyzer
areas.summary: A Wireshark-style record list over every search result, with a display-filter language, a field tree, the raw record and statistics.

features.name: Display filter
features.text: Type a filter such as type == 'DMR' && dbm > -80 and press Enter or Apply. The box turns green when it parses and red with the error when it doesn't, and the count reads N displayed of M.

features.name: Filter language
features.text: Any record field by name, plus short names such as freq, type, dbm, dist, src, call, ssid, mac, band and time, with comparisons, contains, matches, and, or, not and brackets. Type and time read what their columns show.

features.name: Filter presets
features.text: Nine ready filters: Digital land mobile, Strong (> -70 dBm), Within 1 mi, Repeaters, My captures only, Open Wi-Fi, Cellular, Public safety, and Expired / removed licences.

features.name: Order and row count
features.text: Order by time, distance, frequency or level, ascending or descending. Show 500, 3,000, 10,000 or 25,000 rows; Show 3,000 more adds the next batch.

features.name: Columns and row colours
features.text: Twelve columns (No., Time, seconds from the first, Source, Type, Freq MHz, Ident, Name, dBm, Dist mi, Band, Info), each a chip to show or hide. Rows are tinted by signal type with a legend, and dBm and distance cells carry bars.

features.name: Keep only this, Drop this
features.text: Alt+click a source, type, frequency, ident or band cell to keep only that value; Alt+Shift+click drops it. A plain click or tap gives Keep only this and Drop this buttons, and both work on towers, 911 centres and Unknown rows.

features.name: Field tree and raw record
features.text: Click a row for its fields in folding sections (position, radio with each emission designator decoded, identification, licensee, antenna, your labels, the source's own fields) beside the raw JSON. Arrow keys step through rows; a double-click opens Details.

features.name: Statistics view
features.text: The filtered records as a source-to-signal-type hierarchy with shares, an IO graph of records and average dBm over capture time, and the top 300 endpoints by call sign, MAC, cell or ID with min, average and max dBm, first and last seen.

areas.name: Dashboard
areas.summary: Counts, a map and charts of the current results; its bars filter every tab.

features.name: Count cards
features.text: Six cards: items shown, distinct frequencies, distinct locations, signal types, strongest dBm (measured or predicted) and captured points.

features.name: Results map
features.text: Every result with a location as a dot in its signal type's colour, with a scale bar. With a pin it adds dashed distance rings and the search circle and fits the radius.

features.name: Bars that filter every tab
features.text: A click on a Signal types, Bands or Categories bar or slice toggles that filter on every tab. A Sources bar shows that source alone; the same bar again puts the other sources back.

features.name: Level, distance and time charts
features.text: Histograms of signal level and of distance from the pin, each with its median and mean marked, plus capture activity over time, or licence grants by year when no capture has a time.

features.name: Top names
features.text: The top licensees, names or SSIDs by entry count. These bars don't filter: a tap shows a name that was cut short in full.

features.name: Chart settings
features.text: Histogram bins (10 to 80), how many to show in lists (8 to 50), and levels as measured plus predicted, measured only or predicted only. A chart with nothing to count says so and how to widen the search.

areas.name: Topology
areas.summary: A graph of who holds what and where: licensees, licences, frequencies, sites, towers, cell sites and frequencies several users share.

features.name: Logical view
features.text: Licensee to licence (call sign) to frequency, with a repeater's output linked to its input by a dashed amber line. Wi-Fi networks link to their access points, and RepeaterBook entries sit under one Ham/GMRS repeaters group.

features.name: Physical view
features.text: Nodes at their real positions around the pin: FCC towers as triangles, transmitter sites linked to their tower and to their licensees, and each licensee at the centre of its sites.

features.name: Co-channel view
features.text: Each frequency used by two or more licensees, or at two or more sites, becomes a node with red links to each user; nearer users draw thicker links.

features.name: Cell sites in the graph
features.text: Crowd cell readings group into cell sites by the eNB or gNB number in the cell ID: linked to their carrier in Logical, placed on the FCC tower within 200 m in Physical. Old 3G, CDMA and GSM cells show grey.

features.name: Layout and node cap
features.text: Force, Rings by links, Hierarchy or Grid layouts in Logical and Co-channel. Draw up to 300, 900, 2,000 or 5,000 nodes; cell sites take at most half, nearest first, so licences and towers still show, and a trimmed graph says so.

features.name: Zoom and pan
features.text: The plain mouse wheel scrolls the page; Ctrl+wheel or a pinch zooms at the cursor. Drag to pan; the toolbar has minus, plus with the zoom percentage, Fit, 1:1 and full screen.

features.name: Find and highlight
features.text: Find jumps to a node by name, picked from a list of up to 3,000, and lights up its links. Clicking a node dims everything else; clicking the background clears it.

features.name: PNG and legend
features.text: Download PNG saves the graph at twice screen size. A legend under the graph explains the shapes and line styles.

features.name: Towers with their carriers
features.text: Under the graph, each FCC tower in the area with its owner, height and distance, every carrier's cell sites and cells on it, and the bands each carrier is licensed for there. Click a tower for its sites, cells and channel numbers.

areas.name: Site profile
areas.summary: A one-page dossier of the area: counts, the mission's watch list, breakdowns, where the sites are, the strongest and nearest, and a printable prep sheet.

features.name: Header and cards
features.text: The pin and radius or county, the active mission, the FCC data date and a filters-on tag, then up to nine cards with their definitions: licensed frequencies, licensees, towers, repeaters, digital-capable share, nearest licensed site, strongest level, captured and crowd points.

features.name: Watch list check
features.text: Each watch-list frequency of the active mission is checked against every result, filters or not: licences, repeater inputs, captures and crowd data within its tolerance (12.5 kHz unless set), closest 25 first. With nothing there it says so in green.

features.name: Breakdown bars
features.text: By signal type, band, category and top licensees, counted by frequencies, licensees or entries, each with its share. Clicking any bar filters every tab; a licensee bar sets the agency filter.

features.name: Where the sites are
features.text: With a pin, a polar chart of 16 compass directions by 4 distance rings, darker where more sites sit, naming the busiest cell and the busiest direction.

features.name: Strongest and nearest
features.text: With a pin, the strongest signals by the chosen level, measured or free-space estimate, and the nearest licensed sites and towers with distance, bearing, frequency, station class and height. Click a row for its Details window.

features.name: Profile settings
features.text: Breakdowns count by frequencies, licensees or entries; show top 8 to 50; lists of 10 to 50 rows; rank levels by measured plus predicted, measured only or predicted only.

features.name: Prep sheet
features.text: Export, Prep sheet opens Site profile and prints a field checklist: every frequency in the results with input, source, type, emission, ERP, distance, bearing, level and an empty Heard? box. It notes that federal users aren't in FCC ULS.

areas.name: Agencies
areas.summary: A RadioReference-style directory of the area's FCC licences: category, then licensee, then frequencies.

features.name: Categories and licensees
features.text: Licences grouped by category, largest first, each licensee a panel with its frequency and licence counts, nearest distance and radio services. Panels start open in categories of six or fewer, or when Find is used.

features.name: Frequency table
features.text: One row per frequency and call sign, nearest site kept: MHz, input, band, station type, alpha tag (ticked when verified), mode, tone, description, sites, nearest distance and direction, ERP, call sign. Click a row to add tags and tones.

features.name: Sort, find, expand
features.text: Sort licensees A to Z, nearest first or by most frequencies. Find matches licensee, call sign, MHz or alpha tag as you type; Expand all and Collapse all open or fold every panel.

features.name: Expired licences too
features.text: With the expired and removed licences layer on, those licences sit in the directory beside the active ones.

areas.name: Spectrum
areas.summary: An analyzer-style view of every frequency in the results at its exact position, with the band plan, markers and each carrier's licensed blocks.

features.name: One line per frequency
features.text: Every frequency in the results at its exact position down to kHz; entries on one frequency merge into one line coloured by the most common signal type. Measured entries draw thicker with a red triangle on top.

features.name: Range, zoom and pan
features.text: Type From and To, pick one of 14 band presets, or use minus, plus and the arrows. Drag across the plot to zoom into it, Ctrl+wheel zooms at the cursor, Shift+drag pans; the narrowest view is 5 kHz.

features.name: Overview strip
features.text: A strip under the plot shows the whole result with the current window shaded; click or drag it to move the window at the same width.

features.name: Scale and height
features.text: Auto switches to a log axis when the range spans more than 20 times, or pick Linear or Log. Height shows entry counts, the strongest predicted dBm or the strongest measured dBm.

features.name: Band plan and channel widths
features.text: A band-plan strip above the plot names each allocation where it is wide enough. Channel widths draws each signal at its emission's real width once zoomed in far enough.

features.name: Hover readout
features.text: Hovering a line shows its frequency and width, how many entries and how many measured, the strongest predicted and measured levels, the signal types and up to four names.

features.name: Known signals
features.text: A strip of Signal ID Wiki signals whose frequencies fall in view; hover it for what could be on that frequency. Personal build only: Cody's PC and the admin login on the server.

features.name: Spectrum markers
features.text: Click the plot (it snaps to the nearest signal) or type a frequency to drop a marker. The table gives each one's kHz offset from M1, a name, what's within 6.25 kHz, and a button adding it to the mission's watch list.

features.name: Carrier blocks by frequency
features.text: Under the plot, each carrier's licensed blocks for the area's cell sites: band, block, downlink and uplink MHz, 3GPP band, sites here and a bar on one shared scale. Marked licensed, not measured.

areas.name: Cell sites
areas.summary: The cell sites around the pin: crowd and survey cells grouped into sites and matched to FCC towers, each site's public record, and the carriers' modelled coverage at the pin.

features.name: Cells grouped into sites
features.text: Cells from OpenCelliD, your own captures and, in the owner's personal build, WiGLE are decoded to their global cell ID and grouped into sites: one LTE eNB, 5G gNB or 3G RNC each.

features.name: Carrier names
features.text: Each site's carrier comes from its network code: the big carriers by brand, regional carriers by name from the US IMSI administrator's list, and a US code on no one's list says so.

features.name: Tower match and sector directions
features.text: Each site is matched to the nearest FCC-registered tower within 1 km, with its owner, height and the licensees on it. A sector's direction is an estimate, from the tower toward where the crowd saw that cell.

features.name: Fills in by itself
features.text: An area with no cells kept gets OpenCelliD's cells within about 3 miles of the pin, once, and says why when it can't. An area fetched in the last month isn't asked again, and every login shares 25 areas a day.

features.name: Whole-US cells
features.text: With the whole-US OpenCelliD load switched on in Data & updates, cell sites show anywhere with no per-area fetch, each cell with its first and last seen dates and its PCI or PSC.

features.name: Filters, By site, By tower
features.text: Operator, Technology and a Find box (cell ID, eNB, tower owner) narrow the list, under a line counting sites, cells, tower matches and towers nearby. By tower lists each FCC tower with every carrier's sites, cells and licensed bands.

features.name: A site's record
features.text: Click a site for its sectors (cell ID, PCI or PSC, estimated direction, range, samples, last seen, coverage per sector), its FCC tower and licensees, everything else on that tower, and links to CellMapper, OpenCelliD and WiGLE.

features.name: PCI and PSC
features.text: Each sector shows its physical cell ID (LTE, 5G) or scrambling code (3G) where the crowd heard it, and not heard where it didn't.

features.name: Cellular licence at the site
features.text: The 800 MHz cellular licence filed for that tower, or within 150 m when there's no tower: call sign, licensee on the licence, A or B block, frequencies each way, ERP and antenna height.

features.name: Bands and channels per site
features.text: Every block the site's carrier is licensed for in the county, downlink and uplink MHz, worked out to channel numbers for its technology: EARFCN, NR-ARFCN, UARFCN, ARFCN or CDMA channels. TDD and downlink-only bands say so; marked licensed, not measured.

features.name: What a scan adds
features.text: A fold-out says what only a scanner or phone capture brings (each sector's channel, bandwidth, broadcast settings, signal and timing) and that nothing identifying a person is collected.

features.name: Old cells flagged
features.text: A cell the crowd hasn't reported in two years shows the year it was last seen, and one missing from OpenCelliD's current US file says so: AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon shut 3G and CDMA down in 2022.

features.name: Carrier coverage at the pin
features.text: Each carrier the FCC Broadband Map shows covering the pin, with technology, speeds and strongest modelled signal. How modelled shows the frequencies in its filed link budgets, one row per band, and the tools, terrain, clutter and calibration used.

features.name: FCC checks and fixed wireless
features.text: For the pin's 0.7 km² cell, the FCC's resolved challenges, verifications and audits of carrier coverage with outcome and date, and the licensed, unlicensed and LBR fixed wireless offered there with best speeds.

features.name: Cell site exports
features.text: Download CSV (one row per cell, with its tower, PCI or PSC and the carrier's licensed bands), KML or an ATAK package of the sites in the list.

features.name: Import an OpenCelliD file
features.text: Load an OpenCelliD country file (CSV or .csv.gz; 310 to 316 for the US). It keeps the cells inside the states set in Data & updates and says how many it kept.

features.name: Cell sites on other tabs
features.text: Search, Area report, Analyzer, Dashboard, Site profile and Agencies list the area's cell sites: carrier, technology, site, tower, distance, bands licensed here, cells, PCI or PSC heard, last seen. A row opens to its full record.

features.name: Reads only what's kept
features.text: The panel on the other tabs never fetches cells: with none kept it points to Open Cell sites, which finds them once. On the full web version it stays hidden when the field pack holds no cells.

areas.name: Mission
areas.summary: Field work around one area: missions with targets and settings, captures and receivers, the field log, compare, replay, when heard, lines of bearing, and Find a signal at the top.

features.name: Find a signal
features.text: A fold-out at the top of Mission for hunting a rogue booster or interferer from a phone: give the frequency and match width (one channel to 5 MHz), then at each stop save your position, the level and a direction if you can.

features.name: Where it probably is
features.text: From 3 stops with a level, or crossing directions, it gives the best guess: how far and which way from you, plus or minus metres, warmer or colder than the last stop, a map, and Put the pin there.

features.name: Phone compass, true north
features.text: The phone's compass reads flat (top edge) or upright (camera side), averaged over the last second with its spread shown. Every bearing turns to true north with NOAA's World Magnetic Model 2025 at your position; a typed bearing says magnetic or true.

features.name: Steady compass gate
features.text: A compass direction saves only when the last half second agrees within 5° and the phone doesn't call its compass uncalibrated or rough. Save waits up to 4 seconds, then says why and offers Save the level only.

features.name: Stop counter and next stop
features.text: A counter works toward 8 stops, then 10, and says how much tighter the next ones make the estimate. After 3 stops a purple ring shows where to stand next; with directions, once the estimate is within 150 m.

features.name: Bad bearings left out
features.text: From 8 bearings, directions pointing well away from the rest are left out of the fix when most lines agree, and the panel says how many. Find a signal and Lines of bearing both use it.

features.name: Mission list
features.text: A mission holds a name, status, operator, dates, objective, area, target signal types and bands, a watch list and default layers. Picking one makes it active, loads its area and layers and runs the search.

features.name: Watch list and targets
features.text: Planned or suspect frequencies, each with a tolerance and label, checked on Site profile against licences, repeater inputs, captures and crowd data. One button applies the mission's target types and bands as filters.

features.name: Collection and heatmap settings
features.text: Max GPS error, ignore below a dBm, an SDR peak threshold and the GPS track window apply to every capture imported afterwards. Heatmap resolution, how levels combine and opacity are set per mission, and crowd layers refresh with automatic updates.

features.name: Mission log in words
features.text: Every settings change is logged with its time and reads in words (not set, on, off); a setting that only went from not set to off isn't logged. Add your own notes to the same log.

features.name: Import field captures
features.text: WiGLE or Kismet CSV, GPX tracks, rtl_power or hackrf_sweep sweeps, analyzer CSV and KML or KMZ, detected by themselves. Each reading's type comes from the file, a nearby licence, its bandwidth or the band plan, with a summary of what was dropped.

features.name: Placed from the GPS track
features.text: An analyzer CSV with no coordinates is placed from the mission's GPS track by time, within 30 seconds unless set. Place un-positioned points at the mission pin covers the rest; a file nothing can place is refused with the reason.

features.name: Receiver on each capture
features.text: The import asks which receiver took the captures, whether it was calibrated and when; each capture's row shows it and the pencil edits it. Calibrated levels grade A in the Area report, uncalibrated C.

features.name: Field log
features.text: A quick reading at your GPS position or the pin: frequency, dBm, an optional bearing, type and notes. Auto-identify checks the nearest active licence within 6.25 kHz and 40 miles, then the band plan; the personal build adds Signal ID Wiki suggestions.

features.name: Mission exports
features.text: Mission KML with the points and GPS tracks, and a Mission CSV of the captures and the licences and towers in the area.

features.name: Compare with another survey
features.text: Pick a baseline mission and a level change of 3 to 15 dB to list what's new, what's gone and what changed level. Signals match by MAC or cell ID, else by 6.25 kHz channel and type; SDR sweep levels aren't compared.

features.name: Mission replay
features.text: The mission's readings on a map in time order with play and a slider, at 1 minute to 6 hours a second, showing the last minute up to everything so far, with the GPS track behind. Quiet stretches are skipped.

features.name: When heard
features.text: A 24-hour wheel with a ring per weekday shows when readings, or different signals, are heard, with the busiest hours and bars by weekday and by hour, in local time.

features.name: Lines of bearing
features.text: Every reading with a direction (Find a signal stops, field log bearings, an imported bearing, azimuth or DOA column) draws as a line, grouped by signal. The fix gives its quality, average miss and widest crossing, with Put the pin on the fix.

features.name: Bearing error ellipse
features.text: The fix draws as a 95% error ellipse with its size, such as 368 m by 260 m, assuming bearings good to 5° or what the lines' own misses show when worse. Lines crossing at a shallow angle stretch it.

features.name: One filter over time
features.text: A Signal box narrows Replay, When heard and Lines of bearing to one frequency (within 12.5 kHz), a type such as P25, or words in the label.

areas.name: DAS
areas.summary: Runs in-building public safety (ERCES / BDA) and commercial cellular DAS jobs from the first lead to the annual retest.

features.name: Board by stage
features.text: Every job is a card in one of eight columns, Lead to Closed. A card shows its next step and due date, compliance dates on file, the AHJ and the retest countdown; drag it to another column to move it.

features.name: Needs you
features.text: One list above the board, most urgent first: dates coming due, overdue next steps, an unconfirmed code, missing consent or booster registration, licence changes, replies to mark, BDA alarms and calibration reminders. Show all opens everything past the first 8.

features.name: New job
features.text: + New job makes a job at Lead and opens it, placed at the search panel's pin when one is set. One press makes one job, however fast it is clicked.

features.name: Job list
features.text: The same jobs as a table: job, stage, address, AHJ, next step, due, retest due and last update. Click a row to open the job; Find filters it like the board.

features.name: Contact list
features.text: One contact list for every job: name, organisation, role, phone, email and notes, typed straight into the table. Import reads CSV, Excel, vCard and Google or Outlook exports and skips contacts already there; export as CSV or vCard.

features.name: Find across DAS
features.text: The Find box filters the board by name, address, AHJ and client, and from two letters searches every field in every job, the contacts, the log, job files and the DAS research.

features.name: Import and export jobs
features.text: Import job reads one or many jobs exported from DAStastic. Jobs CSV gives one row per job with its dates and checks; All jobs JSON and each job's Job JSON carry everything except the log.

features.name: Example jobs
features.text: Add example jobs makes four fictional jobs: an ERCES office at Acceptance, a cellular warehouse at Design, and both again finished and In service. On an example job, each step says what it's for and what to look at.

features.name: How a DAS job moves
features.text: A panel on the board walks the eight stages: what happens in each and which job steps do it.

features.name: Job steps
features.text: A job's steps run in work order: Overview, Fault chart, Pre-survey, Plans, Requirements, Existing system, Design, Materials, Commissioning, Grid test, Screening, PIM / sweeps / fiber, Files, Log and Report. Step by step opens the job on Start.

features.name: Delete a job
features.text: Delete job removes the job and keeps its folder, renamed _deleted with the date. Job numbers are never reused, so no later job shows a deleted job's files.

features.name: Walk me through
features.text: It reads the job, shows by stage what's on file and what's missing, and opens each place from the first gap. Step waits for Next; Auto moves on when the record shows a step done; physical checks wait for a person.

features.name: Run it for me
features.text: One press does the desk work (outline, NSI, AHJ, floors, channel plan, terrain, cell sites, emails), filling only empty fields. Its AHJ and channel plan clear no gate until someone presses Looks right; each step undoes; nothing is sent.

features.name: Next step from the file
features.text: The board, the job, the gates and Walk me through read one next step from the job's record; a typed Next step wins. A move the file supports shows as a Move button, and In service shows the date the system owes.

features.name: Stage gates
features.text: Moving a job forward lists what the stage still needs, such as the pin, the AHJ and a confirmed Code check at Lead, each with a fix. A typed reason moves it anyway, logged; moves back and to Closed pass.

features.name: Fault chart
features.text: 38 charts, 14 for running a job by stage and 24 for faults, walked one question at a time with the signal path, limits and print sheets. On a job it opens at the job's stage and logs each step.

features.name: No lost edits
features.text: When two people save one job, changes to different fields merge; the same field changed both ways asks Keep theirs, Keep yours or See both, and the rest of the save goes through.

features.name: Change history
features.text: Log › History lists every change with who and when, with Undo for one change and Restore to here for the whole job. Both save as one more revision, so nothing leaves the history.

features.name: Sharing a job
features.text: Log › Sharing opens a job to the team or to named logins at View, Edit or AHJ review. An AHJ reviewer sees only shared jobs and can Accept or Return the report; read-only links stay off until an admin turns them on.

features.name: Watch a grid test live
features.text: The review page an AHJ reviewer or a read-only link opens shows each square as the tester taps it: it checks every 10 seconds while it's open and redraws, keeping your place, and says when it last changed. While you're writing a comment it offers the new readings instead of redrawing. It stops after 6 hours on the page.

features.name: Schedule a watch
features.text: On a job, the admin picks a day, a start, how long and who, and DAStastic opens Google Calendar with the event filled in: the title, the guests, and the way in (a read-only link, or the review page for watchers with a login). Add Google Meet and save in Calendar to send the invites; DAStastic sends nothing.

features.name: Job files
features.text: Drop or choose plans, drawings, PDFs, photos, letters and test exports into the job's Files, each listed with its kind, size and date. Deleting a file is final, except on the PC, where Drive keeps it 30 days.

features.name: Job log
features.text: A dated record per job: add a note for a site visit, an AHJ call or a punch item. DAStastic adds field changes, files added, gate overrides, quote requests, sealed reports, licence changes and fault chart steps.

features.name: Building on the Overview
features.text: Client, address, pin, floors, floor area, construction, AHJ, code basis, next step, due date, value and notes. Picking an address moves the pin in the same save, with Undo; a typed address a mile or more off offers to move it.

features.name: Compliance dates
features.text: Seven dates, where a date means done: licensee consent, FCC Class B registration, AHJ permit, design approved, monitoring to the fire alarm panel, acceptance passed and battery test. Acceptance sets the retest a year on; a cellular-only job drops three.

features.name: People on a job
features.text: Pick a contact for each role: AHJ / fire marshal, building owner, radio system owner, general contractor, subcontractor and our technician. The roles fill the letters, emails and the report.

features.name: Testing details
features.text: The Overview's Testing panel holds the tester, FCC GROL, NICET, test dates, booster class (A, B or not chosen) and the instruments as model, serial and calibration date. All of it prints on the AHJ report.

features.name: Equipment & people
features.text: A firm-wide list of instruments with their calibration and certificates, and people with their licences and credentials. Picking one copies it onto the job, past readings keep the calibration they were taken under, and each gets one reminder instead of one per job.

features.name: Building from the NSI
features.text: Look up building (NSI) asks the USACE National Structure Inventory for occupancy, stories, square feet, basement, year built, height and people by day and night, each marked an estimate with its source. It fills only empty fields.

features.name: DAS Data & links
features.text: Each source the DAS tab reads with its freshness and key, one automatic-update switch and Update all DAS data now, terrain around every job, missing building outlines, and links to codes, AHJ guidelines, FCC look-ups and the research.

features.name: Systems around the building
features.text: Every public safety system within a set radius (15 mi to start): agency, call sign linked to ULS, trunked or conventional, technology, downlink and uplink channels, and the donor site with distance and true and magnetic bearing.

features.name: Systems in order, with Find
features.text: Government trunked and 700/800 MHz systems come first, then other agencies' trunked systems, other agency systems and other licences, each under a heading. Channels past the sixth fold under +N more, and Find narrows the list to a channel, call sign or agency.

features.name: Realistic levels inside
features.text: Each system shows outside, inside and margin twice: a realistic Okumura-Hata estimate (suburban unless set to urban or open land) with the licensed antenna height, pattern and cached terrain, and free space as the best case. The verdict uses the realistic figure.

features.name: Building loss by P.2109
features.text: Building loss starts from ITU-R P.2109 for this building, worked out from its type, size and, after an NSI look-up, its year. NIST TN 1552 presets and a typed figure sit beside it, and the 90 dB underground preset says it's a judgement.

features.name: Channel warnings
features.text: A ⚠ beside a channel opens a pop-up with what it means and what to do: simulcast from several sites (delay interference), the commercial ESMR band next to 800 MHz, or FirstNet Band 14, which needs written authorization.

features.name: Channel plan
features.text: Tick the systems the AHJ requires, or press Tick fire, police, EMS, 911. The ticked systems' channels save with the job as its channel plan, so Design, the letters and the Report work without the FCC data.

features.name: Bands a booster must pass
features.text: For the ticked systems, each band's lowest and highest frequency and channel count, downlink and uplink, with the Class A and Class B rules and the ESMR and Band 14 cautions.

features.name: Boosters granted
features.text: Matches FCC equipment grants to every chosen band, newest grant first, filtered by class (Part 90 A or B, Part 20) and the strongest band's power, and says when no single device covers all the bands.

features.name: Federal systems
features.text: The list says federal systems aren't on it, because NTIA assigns them, and asks whether any serve the building and who said so. The answer prints on ER-1 of the design submittal.

features.name: Terrain paths
features.text: ⛰ Terrain paths checks line of sight from each donor site to the roof (the building's height plus a 3 m mast): clear, partly blocked or blocked, with the loss and the worst point, for the ticked systems or the 20 strongest.

features.name: Donor aiming sheet
features.text: A printable sheet per donor site: distance, true and magnetic bearing, elevation angle allowing for the earth's curve, terrain clearance, expected level at the roof, simulcast, and whether the building is off the site antenna's main beam. The ATAK export carries it.

features.name: Pre-survey exports and map
features.text: Channel plan CSV, Systems CSV, KML with the sites, donor lines and building outline, and an ATAK package whose donor markers say where to aim. A map shows the building, its outline and lines to each donor site.

features.name: Licensee consent letters
features.text: One letter per licensee asking consent to retransmit under 47 CFR 90.219, listing its channels, addressed to the licence's own FCC contact; with no record, nothing is guessed. Print it, save it as a PDF, or email it.

features.name: Licensees in the passbands
features.text: Every licensee near the building whose channels fall inside the booster's passbands, downlink and uplink apart: whether Class B or a 75 kHz Class A filter passes it, its FCC contact, consent status, and a letter or email each.

features.name: FCC licence watch
features.text: Each job's licences are snapshotted and checked after every FCC update: gone, expired, renamed, channels or sites changed, expiring within 90 days, or another licensee on or next to its channels. Changes stay on Needs you and the job until marked handled.

features.name: Existing system audit
features.text: A job step for a booster already in the building: a 14-item sourced checklist and findings such as an unregistered Class B, missing consent, ESMR or Band 14 passed, or no oscillation shutdown, sent to Needs you and the report.

features.name: Tunnels near the building
features.text: Look for tunnels within 400 m asks OpenStreetMap for road and rail tunnels near the building, with length, distance and the standard that applies: NFPA 502 for road, NFPA 130 for rail and transit.

features.name: Cellular carriers at the building
features.text: For AT&T, Verizon, T-Mobile, FirstNet and any carrier measured: Broadband Map coverage, the closest known cell site within 5 mi, a rooftop donor reading against a −85 dBm target and −95 dBm minimum, and the approval path with asked and consent dates.

features.name: Carrier consent letters
features.text: A consent letter per carrier under 47 CFR 20.21(c), printed or emailed, with T-Mobile pre-addressed to its rebroadcast agreements address and each carrier's known consent process beside it.

features.name: Consumer booster bands
features.text: A band measured here that a consumer booster can't carry (600 MHz, WCS, 2.5 GHz, CBRS, 3.45 GHz / C-band, AWS-4) gets a warning pointing to an industrial booster with carrier consent; B66 says only its AWS-1 part qualifies.

features.name: Spectrum each carrier holds
features.text: For the building's county, each carrier's licensed blocks by band in MHz, downlink and uplink, from the FCC's market licences; a licence split inside its market is marked. Leases aren't in the files, so 2.5 GHz isn't shown.

features.name: Who holds a frequency
features.text: Type a frequency from a scan into Who holds and it names who is licensed for it in this county, the band and block, and whether it's the uplink or the downlink.

features.name: Find cell sites here
features.text: When no cell site is known around the building, Find cell sites here loads OpenCelliD's crowd-mapped cells about 3 miles around the pin and keeps them for next time.

features.name: Screening step
features.text: A step after the Grid test judges each public safety reading against its instrument's published accuracy: likely pass, too close to call or likely fail. It knows PCTEL IBflex, Anritsu S412E, Epiq PRiSM and Nextivity COMPASS XR; uncalibrated readings aren't judged.

features.name: What Screening says to fix
features.text: It lists squares to fix before the witnessed walk, squares inside the instrument's accuracy and readings not judged. Squares are striped so a call never reads as a result; the score and Report don't change; Screening CSV holds every call.

features.name: AHJ presets
features.text: 26 presets set the downlink level, DAQ, general and critical percentages, battery hours and grid rule: five model-code sets (IFC 2021, IFC 2024, Strict, Older NFPA 72, Florida 9th) and 21 AHJs' own documents, each with its source.

features.name: The job's own numbers
features.text: Any number can be changed per job, and an edited preset keeps its name, marked edited. Where each number comes from shows the section behind every figure, or says the policy doesn't state it.

features.name: SINR and BER bar
features.text: The SINR and BER pass bar comes from the AHJ's policy where it gives one (San Diego, LA County and Douglas County: 20 dB). Without one it is 18 dB with 2.5% BER for DAQ 3.0, or 2% for DAQ 3.4.

features.name: Uplink in every square
features.text: Where the AHJ asks for an uplink reading in every square, a square with only a downlink reading counts as untested, never as a pass, and the floor lists those squares. Seven presets switch it on; any job can tick it.

features.name: Grid rule
features.text: Each job picks how its floors are judged: IFC 510.5.4 failed areas, or percentages only for AHJs that follow NFPA alone.

features.name: What the code asks
features.text: Fifteen rows with the job's numbers filled in: signal, audio quality and its SINR / BER, uplink, coverage, grid test, test radio, isolation, standby power, equipment, supervision, noise at the agency site, annual and five-year tests, FCC and people.

features.name: AHJ final authority
features.text: Requirements and the Code check say it plainly: the AHJ enforces what's in the adopted code, can ask for more, and what it tells you in writing wins over anything on the page.

features.name: Critical areas
features.text: Tick the named critical areas in the building (fire command center, fire pump room, exit stairs, exit passageways, elevator cars apart from their lobbies, standpipe cabinets and more) or add your own. Each becomes its own row on the Grid test.

features.name: Licensee consent processes
features.text: Nine licensees' own consent processes from the research, each with its term where known: Michigan MPSCS, Ohio MARCS, California CRIS, Maryland FiRST, Broward ORCAT, Douglas County, Fairfax, PSERN and FirstNet Band 14.

features.name: Cellular coverage targets
features.text: Six presets set RSRP, RSRP from 3.3 GHz, SINR and coverage %: Common, Cooper University Health, Providence normal and failover, SOLiD and MCF. Tick which carriers must pass; cellular results never count toward the public safety result.

features.name: Code check
features.text: On each job's Overview: the state's rule for the building and how far it was read, searches for the local amendment and the fire department's guideline, questions for the AHJ as a drafted email or call sheet, and who confirmed it, and when.

features.name: AHJ guess
features.text: Suggest the AHJ names the fire departments covering the address from the USFA National Fire Department Registry, which stopped taking updates in June 2026 and says so. Use as AHJ fills the job's AHJ and adds the department as its AHJ contact.

features.name: AHJ book
features.text: What one job confirmed about an AHJ is offered on the next job in the same place or with the same AHJ, with its date, and reads as old after 12 months. It fills blank answers only and never clears the Code check.

features.name: Link budget per band
features.text: One budget per band of the channel plan, worked at its highest downlink and uplink frequency, stage by stage: from the signal at the roof to the far edge, and from the portable radio back to the agency's site.

features.name: Defaults with their sources
features.text: Every empty input shows its default and where it came from: the link-budget research, 47 CFR 90.219, TSB-88, P.1238 or the job's own requirement. Clearing a field puts the default back.

features.name: Passive network
features.text: Add cable runs with their loss per 100 ft at the band's frequency, add parts with a fixed loss, or pull the job's bill-of-materials cable lines in with Add the cable runs from Materials.

features.name: Link budget checks
features.text: Downlink at the far edge, uplink level and margin at the agency's receiver, uplink and server ERP within 5 W, donor port, uplink gain cap, 90.219 noise, noise at the site, isolation and BDA headroom. Without a roof reading, downlink checks stay open.

features.name: Cable stop band
features.text: The check Every cable carries this band fails when a radiating cable runs inside its stop band (RLKU: 650 to 750, 1330 to 1430 and 2025 to 2100 MHz), and that run shows no loss figure.

features.name: Cellular link budget
features.text: 17 LTE and 5G bands, B71 600 MHz to n77 C-band, each with its holders, run in RSRP against the job's cellular target, with the consumer booster caps (17 dBm down, 30 dBm up), isolation and headroom.

features.name: P.1238 N by frequency
features.text: The in-building path is ITU-R P.1238 (site-specific) or free space plus walls. A band's default N comes from the P.1238 office row nearest its frequency: 33 at 700 to 900 MHz, 30 for PCS, AWS and above; a job's own N wins.

features.name: Drawn walls count once
features.text: On P.1238, a path with drawn walls takes the larger of P.1238 and free space plus walls, because N already allows for walls. The older sum stays one pick away under Drawn walls, and each floor sheet names its model.

features.name: Antennas on the plan
features.text: Click to place server antennas on each floor plan. Each one's gain and feed loss can be set; feed loss starts from the link budget's passive loss to the farthest antenna.

features.name: Wall losses
features.text: Twelve wall types. Each wall's loss at the band's frequency comes from NIST NISTIR 6055 measurements or Cardinal low-E data, with the ITU-R P.2040 model only where nothing was measured; a loss can be typed in.

features.name: Predicted coverage
features.text: Each floor's heat map takes the best antenna's level at each point: green 5 dB or more over the requirement, amber within 5 dB, red below, with the share of the floor at target and the squares predicted to pass.

features.name: Floor to floor
features.text: Antennas on the floors above and below reach each floor through the slab, using ITU-R P.1238 floor penetration loss.

features.name: Fit to the walk
features.text: Every walk point is set against the prediction, with the mean error and spread. Fit to the walk fits P.1238's N, each wall type's loss and the floor loss to the readings on every floor; Back to the defaults undoes it.

features.name: Per-antenna budget and caps
features.text: Each antenna's port power, EIRP and ERP against the cap, the weakest point it serves and the uplink from there. Caps presets load Douglas County, Sacramento FPS 32, LA County or San Diego's limits.

features.name: Battery sizing
features.text: Hours come from the job's AHJ or a picked rule (NFPA 1225, IFC 2024, LA County, San Diego, Clark County, Santa Clara, Colorado Springs, FDNY), battery only or with a generator, with the 70% low-battery point and a 20% margin.

features.name: Battery table formats
features.text: The battery sheet prints in the standard per-item format or in the Colorado Springs or FDNY table format, and the submittal shows the hours the job used.

features.name: Intermod check
features.text: IM3 and IM5 products of the plan's channels (and any cellular band) are checked against the uplinks and Class A filters: frequencies to watch under the link budget, and a PIM test plan per band on the job's PIM step.

features.name: PDF plan sheets to floors
features.text: Pick a PDF from the job's files or add one; its pages show as thumbnails, and Save stores a page as that floor's plan image, keeping the page so the wall tools can read its lines.

features.name: Plan set reader
features.text: A plan set's title blocks and sheet index propose the floors, which page is which floor, the scale and width, and the critical areas, each with the words it came from. Ceiling and demolition sheets are skipped; nothing fills without a press.

features.name: Building outline
features.text: Get the building's outline brings the footprint, floors and height from OpenStreetMap, or from Overture Maps where OpenStreetMap has none or doesn't answer, filling only empty fields. Over 128,000 sq ft a floor, it warns that NFPA 1225 splits floors into sectors.

features.name: The building from OpenStreetMap
features.text: Plans shows what OpenStreetMap holds on the building: name, kind, levels above and below ground, height, footprint, wall material, facade, roof and year built. It asks every public server at once, the job's own building first, with Try again.

features.name: Ask for the plans
features.text: A researched request for the plans, filled from the job and the technician contact, with Copy the email. Reference panels cover where plans come from, what AHJs ask for and open building data.

features.name: DXF plans
features.text: On Antennas and coverage, import a DXF floor plan: the drawing becomes the floor's plan at its true width, and lines on wall layers are offered as walls with a material from each layer's name. A DWG is saved as DXF first.

features.name: Walls from the plan
features.text: The wall tools read the plan's own lines, from the PDF or else the image; a phone photo finds none and says draw by hand. Drag along a wall or click its ends; the pointer snaps to ends, crossings and square.

features.name: Snip, Lasso and Smart
features.text: Snip (a box) and Lasso (any loop) find the walls inside in the picked type; Smart types each wall from plan words, stairs and shafts, glazing, hatching, thickness and other floors. Finds show green, amber or grey; Enter adds the sure ones.

features.name: Best tool for the plan
features.text: The 💡 button names the tool that suits this plan, such as Smart snip for a clean PDF or Draw by hand when no lines can be read, and switches to it on a click.

features.name: Wall tool keys
features.text: W walls, A antennas, S snip, L lasso, E remove; Shift flips add and remove; M or 1 to 0 pick the wall type; B and F step band and floor; X snap; Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z undo and redo 30 steps.

features.name: Plan width
features.text: Each floor's real width in feet sets every distance on Design and the Grid test, from the drawing's scale or dimensions; the plan set reader offers the width its scale gives.

features.name: Place grid
features.text: On the Grid test, a floor's plan keeps its own shape: Place grid drags, sizes and turns the grid on it, Fit to plan resets it, and the square size comes from the plan's width.

features.name: Bill of materials
features.text: A part number fills the line from the catalogue. Lines sit in seven install groups (donor and roof, head-end, fiber, remotes, accessories, tools, spares) with subtotals, and each price keeps its date and says when it has moved or gone old.

features.name: Missing and wrong parts
features.text: A completeness check lists what the job's list is missing, each with its reason and source and one click to add it, and warns about a part wrong for this job, such as one that doesn't cover the job's bands.

features.name: Hytera maker note
features.text: A Sinclair or Norsat line gets a Maker note: Hytera owns both, it's on the FCC Covered List, and DA 26-635 bars marketing its gear for public safety. Passive parts are an open question, so it's a note, not a block.

features.name: Kits and revisions
features.text: Save lines as a kit and add the kit to any job. Issue a dated revision of the list with a note, and the list then marks what changed against that revision.

features.name: Customer, technician and AHJ sheets
features.text: One list three ways, on screen, in print and as a real Excel workbook: Customer shows markup and no cost, Technician and AHJ carry no prices anywhere. An order sheet by supplier, at cost, is its own file for the firm.

features.name: iBwave import
features.text: Reads an iBwave equipment list as CSV, Excel or older .xls, finds the columns by name, previews what matched the catalogue and what's already on the list, and adds nothing until you say so.

features.name: Part in hand
features.text: Type the part number off a box in your hand and it says whether this job's list has it, on which line and where it goes, or names the closest part numbers on the list.

features.name: Standard parts
features.text: ★ Add my standard parts adds every part starred in the catalogue at its default quantity, and leaves parts already on the list as they are.

features.name: Parts catalogue
features.text: Import a supplier's price list (CSV, Excel or JSON, dated so older lists build price history), search by part number, maker, supplier or FCC ID, star standard parts with a default quantity and shipping weight, and + BOM a part.

features.name: Boosters from FCC grants
features.text: Every Part 90 Class A and B booster on the kept FCC grants is a part with its FCC ID, class, bands, power and grant date. Every part carries AHJ code fields (UL 2524, class, NEMA, 2-hour, PIM) into the BOM and packet.

features.name: Antenna patterns
features.text: A maker's Planet .msi or .pln file becomes an antenna part with its pattern, drawn as two polar cuts.

features.name: Spec sheets for the AHJ
features.text: Build spec sheets puts each part's sheet in the job's Files, from its kept PDF or public link, and names parts still missing one. BOM + spec sheets (zip) holds them all; its CSV leaves prices out unless you untick the box.

features.name: Spec sheet reader
features.text: A part's spec sheet proposes its code fields (UL listing, frequency ranges, power and more) with the words beside each; Read the spec sheets for this list reads every sheet. A press fills only empty fields; a pending listing proposes nothing.

features.name: Request for quote
features.text: One request from the bill of materials to several suppliers, with need-by date, ship-to and a note. A connected mailbox sends it with the quote sheet attached; otherwise it opens in your own mail. Request numbers are never reused.

features.name: Compare supplier quotes
features.text: Type each line's price and lead time, shipping, validity and quote number, import the supplier's sheet, or apply prices read from an emailed reply. The comparison tags cheapest and fastest, finds the best split, and Use puts the winner on the BOM.

features.name: Supplier price list links
features.text: Each supplier can carry a price list link that is re-read weekly, or on demand with Re-read price lists, plus a ship-from address for shipping estimates.

features.name: Online prices
features.text: Check online prices asks Mouser and Digi-Key for the price at your quantity, stock and lead time, once their free keys are saved. Open requests for quote from the last 60 days are repriced weekly.

features.name: Shipping estimates
features.text: With a Shippo token, Estimate shipping asks UPS, FedEx and USPS for rates from each supplier's ship-from address and puts the cheapest on the quote marked est., the fastest beside it. A supplier's own price stands; over 150 lb is freight.

features.name: Material rules
features.text: Tick the cited ERCES / DAS material rules confirmed for this job. The ticks print in the design submittal and on the test report, which says how many are confirmed.

features.name: Grid per floor
features.text: Grid test sets each floor's squares (20 by default) and columns, and marks squares Do not test or Critical. It warns when a square runs outside 20 to 80 ft across or a floor over 128,000 sq ft needs sectors.

features.name: Readings per channel
features.text: Click a square to enter DL dBm, DL DAQ, SINR, BER, UL dBm and UL DAQ for each channel. The worst calibrated channel decides the square, so it passes only when every channel passes.

features.name: Pass line per reading
features.text: A reading passes at the AHJ's dBm level with DAQ met, or with SINR and BER at the DAQ equivalent set under Requirements.

features.name: Cellular readings kept apart
features.text: LTE and 5G readings (RSRP, RSRQ) stay on the grid and the plan but never count toward the public-safety result.

features.name: Calibrated instruments only
features.text: Taken with names what took the readings: a job instrument, Not calibrated (kept as pre-survey, never scored), or an added PCTEL IBflex, Anritsu S412E, Epiq PRiSM, COMPASS XR or other. Only a calibration within 12 months, or an in-date certificate, counts.

features.name: Unnamed readings fixed at once
features.text: Readings that don't say what took them don't count. The Grid test says how many there are, and Apply to these names the instrument for all of them in one press.

features.name: Reading stands on its calibration
features.text: A reading is judged on the calibration in force when it was taken. A newer certificate never turns an uncounted reading into a counted one, and the server and the page read it the same way.

features.name: Calibration certificates
features.text: Overview, Testing keeps each instrument's certificate from the job's Files with its expiry, warns 30 days ahead, and stops counting readings after it expires. Each certificate goes into the AHJ packet zip.

features.name: Certificate reader
features.text: Read a certificate takes a PDF in the job's Files and proposes the instrument's serial, model, calibration and due dates, or a NICET, FDNY B-03 or manufacturer certificate's expiry, each with the words it came from. Nothing fills until you press.

features.name: Certificate reader guards
features.text: A lab's own standards table is never read as the instrument's, a due date not after the calibration date is flagged, a certificate that doesn't name the job's tester says so, and a scan with no words asks for a person.

features.name: IFC 20 / 40-area scoring
features.text: A floor of 20 areas fails with more than one failed area. With exactly two, Re-divide into 40 areas keeps the readings, dated, and starts 40 squares that pass with at most two failures that don't share an edge.

features.name: Why a floor failed
features.text: The floor card, the rule line and the report say which rule judged the floor and why. Percentages are cut, not rounded, so a fail never reads 95.0%, and other square counts are judged by percentage.

features.name: Critical area readings
features.text: Each critical area named under Requirements gets its own row on the Grid test for DL, DAQ, UL and UL DAQ, with its pass and the instrument it was counted with.

features.name: Import results from any tool
features.text: Import results reads CSV, TSV, Excel, JSON, KML / KMZ, GPX and a Nextivity COMPASS XR Full Signal Report through a column-mapping preview. Rows with no grid go in one square, missing floors are added and critical-area columns mark squares.

features.name: Show a carrier
features.text: Show switches the grid from the public-safety score to one carrier and layer, scored against the job's cellular target by its best cell. A cellular-only job opens on its first required carrier.

features.name: Acceptance baseline
features.text: Save as acceptance baseline keeps today's results as the acceptance test. Later readings show their dB change against it on each square and in the report.

features.name: Acceptance tests
features.text: Grid test records the 12 tests IFC 510.5.4 and NFPA 1225 ask beyond the grid, from gain, isolation and noise floor to battery, supervisory signals, EPO, leakage and BDA identity: each pass, fail or not done, printed on the report.

features.name: Grid exports
features.text: Results CSV gives the reading that decides each square, All readings CSV every reading including cellular in columns the import reads back, and Results JSON the whole result.

features.name: Walk test on the plan
features.text: Grid test, Walk: tap where you stand on the plan, spot by spot or as a continuous walk. Type values, load a COMPASS report for a spot, or import an instrument or survey-app log (G-NetTrack, any CSV), placed by time between taps.

features.name: Walk heat maps
features.text: Each metric, channel, carrier and band gets a heat map against the AHJ's threshold or the job's cellular target. Points CSV, Heat map PNG and Save heat map to Files export it, and the Report prints the heat maps.

features.name: Walk rolls into the grid
features.text: The walk rolls up into the grid squares, one reading per channel taken from the point nearest the square's centre (or its worst or median point), so the IFC score and the Report use it. Only calibrated instruments count.

features.name: Test passes
features.text: Walk the same floors as named passes: BDA off, BDA on, acceptance, annual and five-year, each with its year. Pick the pass the grid and the Report use.

features.name: Compare two passes
features.text: Compare two passes shows a difference heat map per square for the signal shown, each pass's coverage, and Clark County's five-year check of no more than 5% change from the installation.

features.name: Cellular walk passes
features.text: Walk also carries Macro only, CW walk, After optimization and Carrier acceptance passes. A log's phone transmit power and call result columns give the share of points at maximum power, flagged over 10%, and the calls dropped or failed.

features.name: Phone vs instrument
features.text: At five or more spots, the phone and a calibrated instrument read side by side give an offset per band, kept per phone model, that corrects the phone's later readings. Corrected readings never count toward pass or fail.

features.name: Grid tests on the phone
features.text: DAStastic lite enters a grid test square by square with no signal, using the same AHJ profiles and pass rules, and exports a CSV the Grid test imports.

features.name: Public-safety commissioning
features.text: Commissioning walks six steps in the safe order: isolation with the booster off (20 dB over gain), gain, AGC and filter settings per band, the donor-site noise test, oscillation, donor level and source, and a talk-back and near-far log.

features.name: Donor-site noise test
features.text: The noise test reads the agency site booster off, then on, at 10 kHz RBW over a 5-minute average. A rise of 1 dB or more means cut the gain until it's gone, then 3 dB more.

features.name: AHJ numbers in commissioning
features.text: Commissioning grades with NFPA 1225 and IFC 2021 by default, or with San Diego, Orange County Sheriff, San Francisco, Greensboro or McKinney's own numbers, picked from the job's AHJ, each with its source.

features.name: Analyzer files in commissioning
features.text: Type the values, or import an analyzer trace or log as CSV, TSV or Excel: the noise test takes one booster off and one booster on, averaged as power, and the gain step takes a settings table.

features.name: Results fill the acceptance tests
features.text: Each commissioning step's result goes into the acceptance tests the Report prints. An entry typed somewhere else is never overwritten unless you ask, and Print the commissioning record prints every step's readings and result.

features.name: Public safety or cellular switch
features.text: Commissioning has a Public safety | Cellular switch, kept per job. A job whose design carries only LTE and 5G bands, with no public-safety record yet, opens on Cellular; the public-safety record is untouched by the cellular side.

features.name: Cellular commissioning
features.text: Cellular runs eight steps in order: plant passed, baseline noise, downlink CW within 5 dB of the link budget, uplink unity gain and over the air, uplink kept quiet, equal power per MHz per operator, alarms, calls near every antenna.

features.name: Carrier's number wins
features.text: No US carrier publishes its procedure, so the steps follow Viavi's public ones, the MCF Design Guidelines 2025 and one owner's RFP numbers; every threshold takes the carrier's own number where it gives one. Print the cellular record prints it.

features.name: The PIM / sweeps step
