features.text: A job's PIM step is named PIM / sweeps / fiber: sweeps first, then fiber links, then the PIM runs and the job's PIM checklists.

features.name: PIM runs
features.text: Each run records where, band, F1, F2, tone power (43 dBm default), order (IM3, IM5, IM7), PIM dBm, distance to PIM and a note. dBc is PIM minus tone, passing at or below the job's limit, -140 dBc by default.

features.name: PIM checklists in the job
features.text: The PIM research's Pre-test planning, Test setup and verification, Close-out and report, and DAS PIM checklists, ticked per job, with All / None and a done count.

features.name: Sweeps import
features.text: Import return loss, VSWR, distance to fault or insertion loss from Anritsu Site Master and Line Sweep Tools, Keysight FieldFox, Touchstone .s1p / .s2p or a plain two-column table. Each trace is plotted, graded and kept in Files.

features.name: Sweep limits with sources
features.text: Return loss grades against 14 dB (VSWR 1.5:1), an owner's 20 dB, an antenna's 2:1 or your own number. Insertion loss grades against the cable's datasheet loss for its length plus 0.1 dB a connector and a tolerance.

features.name: Fiber links
features.text: Each fiber link's measured loss at 1310 and 1550 nm grades against TIA's maximums (0.75 dB a mated pair, 0.3 dB a splice) or the MCF 2023 draft's formula, and the DAS maker's own budget, with the RF loss it costs.

features.name: OTDR traces
features.text: An OTDR trace (.sor) is kept with its fiber link and goes in the carrier closeout package. DAStastic doesn't read the trace itself.

features.name: Test report
features.text: Report gives PASS, FAIL or Not complete, never PASS with no floors tested. It prints the pass criteria, readings not scored, tester and instruments with calibration, systems covered, a summary by floor with the rule and reason, and a page per floor.

features.name: What else the report carries
features.text: The report adds the acceptance tests, the walk heat maps and pass comparison, sweeps and PIM runs, the commercial cellular section kept apart, and the FCC, OpenCelliD and OpenStreetMap data notices.

features.name: Sign the report
features.text: Sign the report takes the tester's name, title, company, date, statement, the independence statement and a signature drawn with a mouse, pen or finger. Where the AHJ requires a third-party tester and none is signed, the report says so in red.

features.name: Print as final (sealed)
features.text: Print as final seals the report: the server keeps its SHA-256 and a verify code, printed with the date and page number on every page. It warns first when the AHJ packet lists missing items.

features.name: Sealed reports file themselves
features.text: Print as final shows the next step and fills in a dated file name. Drop the saved PDF anywhere: it is checked against its seal, filed on its own job, put in the AHJ packet zip and ticked in Email the AHJ.

features.name: A print that doesn't match
features.text: A made-up code, a real code on other words, an edited print or a changed job goes to the drop spot's Needs a look list with the reason. A filed report whose job changed leaves the package, and the Report says so.

features.name: Verify a report
features.text: Verify a report on the DAS board takes the code from a sealed report's footer and shows what was sealed, its result, date and signer, whether the text matches its hash, and whether the job changed after sealing and which fields.

features.name: Seals ignore data refreshes
features.text: An FCC data update never marks a sealed report as changed, and a job's list of sealed reports follows who can see the job. The signed-out verify page is built and switched off.

features.name: AHJ packet checklist
features.text: Report checks the job against the AHJ's packet list (20 lists, 244 items, each with its section), names what's missing ahead of printing, and prints the packet index at the top of the report.

features.name: Packet files zip
features.text: Packet files (zip) holds the bill of materials as CSV, the AHJ workbook with no prices, every spec sheet, each calibration certificate, and the sealed report's PDF while it still matches the job.

features.name: Design submittal
features.text: Report, Design submittal prints 20 sheets, ER-0 to ER-19: cover and statement of compliance, systems and diagram, link budgets, donor path, isolation, floor designs with test grids, materials, the walk check, battery, consent, qualifications, and installation details.

features.name: Submittal sheet details
features.text: ER-15 to ER-19 cover donor mounting, grounding and surge, pathway survivability, power and the fire alarm interface, with blanks printed for hand entry. ER-0 maps each NFPA 1225 A.18.2.1 item to its sheet, and every page carries project, revision and page.

features.name: System diagram
features.text: The report and submittal draw a one-line diagram from the link budget: agency site, donor antenna and cable, BDA, passive network, server antennas and farthest point, downlink above, uplink below. A carrier job shows rooftop donors per carrier.

features.name: One grid, two technologies
features.text: Per floor, the report shows the public-safety map and the cellular map of the same plan side by side, with a table per square, and keeps two verdicts: cellular never counts toward the ERCES result.

features.name: Cellular reports
features.text: A carrier-only job's report is a commercial cellular coverage test judged per carrier against its target, with rooftop donor readings and carrier approvals. The ERCES packet and acceptance tests stay off it; signing and sealing still apply.

features.name: Carrier closeout packages
features.text: Report shows a card per carrier with 14 closeout items from public lists, each ticked from the job's own records (sweeps, PIM, fiber, commissioning, calls, consent date, files) or by a person, plus the carrier's own items. Each carrier gets one zip.

features.name: Email the AHJ
features.text: Email the AHJ writes to the job's AHJ contact with the job's files to attach, the sealed report's PDF already ticked, and offers a witness test. The reply comes back into the job; without a mailbox it opens in your own mail.

features.name: Lifecycle dates
features.text: Each job tracks the annual test, the NFPA 1225 five-year retest, licensee authorizations, the operating permit, the UL 2524 3rd-edition check, a remodel retest (IFC 510.6.1), calibrations and tester certificates, each sourced, on the Overview and Needs you.

features.name: Carrier job lifecycle
features.text: A carrier-only job tracks each carrier's consent and renewal, the carrier's retest and the owner's maintenance agreement in place of the IFC 510 and NFPA 1225 dates.

features.name: Filing deadlines
features.text: Lifecycle shows when the test report is due to the AHJ (OCSD 30 days and 13 months, Seattle 7, Charleston 30, Denver 30 after each five-year interval) and Clark County, Douglas County and FDNY's five-year rules, each sourced.

features.name: Retest opens itself
features.text: When an annual or five-year test comes due, it opens as a test pass on the Walk; its first reading makes it the test of record for the grid and the Report, compared with acceptance. The acceptance record is never written to.

features.name: Retest dates for a press
features.text: Once the retest's sealed report reads PASS with every square tested this time, the job proposes the last-test date and the report-filed date under Dates to set. Nothing changes until you press Set it, and it says why when it holds back.

features.name: DAS Mail
features.text: DAS, Mail holds Ready to send, your mailbox, and every tagged conversation newest first, each filed under its job, quote or prospect with its status. The Mail button shows how many emails are ready.

features.name: Ready to send
features.text: Emails DAStastic writes wait in groups: BDA alarms, follow-ups after 5 days without a reply, retest and lifecycle reminders, reports due to the AHJ, calibration and certificates, plans requests and prospect first emails. Nothing goes without your click.

features.name: Working the queue
features.text: Preview one to read or edit it, or tick several and Send selected after a confirm. Later puts one off a week, the cross drops it, and a mailbox sends at most 150 an hour.

features.name: Lifecycle reminders
features.text: Every lifecycle date is offered as a written email 90 and 30 days ahead, on the day and every 30 days while overdue, to the owner, licensee or technician it concerns. Calibration and credential reminders come once per instrument or person.

features.name: Pick who, then preview
features.text: Every email box offers the job's people by role, contacts, suppliers and anyone who replied, greets them by first name and shows a preview with Edit and Send. Save as contact and Import contacts (vCard, Google or Outlook CSV) add people.

features.name: Kinds of email
features.text: Email about this job has a Kind of email menu: write it yourself, status to the customer, access and schedule to the general contractor, scope and price to a subcontractor, the design to the AHJ, the plans request, the retest booking.

features.name: Emails this job needs
features.text: Overview and Start list what a job still needs sent: the AHJ's code questions, the radio shop, contractor, design, each licensee and carrier. Ready ones come ticked and one press sends them; a row with no address gets a box.

features.name: Attachments wait for the file
features.text: An email that says something is attached waits until the PDF is in the job's Files, licensees the job doesn't carry start unticked, and a sent email leaves the list.

features.name: A reply does the paperwork
features.text: A consent, carrier or AHJ reply shows on Needs you and the job's email list with Mark given or Mark confirmed; nothing changes until you press. A reply that reads as a refusal says so, and an unknown sender gets no Mark.

features.name: Prospects search
features.text: Prospects finds buildings around a town, an address, a lat, lon, the search pin or a job, within 2, 5, 10, 25 or 50 mi, each ranked by the market research's priority with who to approach and why.

features.name: Building types
features.text: Public and private schools, colleges, hospitals and nursing homes from NCES, IPEDS and CMS; malls, stadiums, hotels, venues, casinos, airports, transit, government buildings, warehouses and garages from Overture; high-rises, tunnels, and buildings under construction from permits.

features.name: High-rises and tunnels
features.text: Find high-rises here finds buildings 75 ft or 7 floors and up from Overture building heights within the radius, at most 10 mi. Find tunnels here adds road and rail tunnels from OpenStreetMap.

features.name: Find email
features.text: Find email reads a building's home and contact pages, robots.txt honoured, and puts its published address on the row; Find emails for the ones shown runs down the list, at most 40 a run. Nothing is guessed.

features.name: RF need per building
features.text: Each building gets an RF need estimate (likely short, close, likely OK) from the deciding agency system's realistic level, the building's loss and each carrier's modelled signal, sorted need first, with land type and map colour pickers.

features.name: Permit and occupancy triggers
features.text: A Trigger column shows each building's strongest building permit or certificate of occupancy from city and county open data (52 datasets, 24 on by default), with a filter for new construction, recent COs, major work or any permit.

features.name: Neighbours' permits marked
features.text: A permit matched only by distance to another building's address reads Nearby with its own address and distance, ranks after the building's own permits, and counts only under Any permit.

features.name: State rule on every building
features.text: Each building shows its state's rule for requiring a system, and Hide no-mandate states drops buildings where nothing can require one. A first email says a system is required only where the state's rule supports it.

features.name: Prospect statuses
features.text: Each building is new, contacted, replied, meeting, won, not interested or do not contact, filtered by status or by name and town. Do not contact removes the Email button, and a status change keeps a found email.

features.name: First emails to buildings
features.text: Email writes a first email with your firm's mailing address and an opt-out, as CAN-SPAM requires, warning until the address is entered. Send from my mail sends it from your connected mailbox; Open in my mail and Copy the text work everywhere.

features.name: Queue first emails
features.text: Queue first emails writes one to every building shown that has an email and hasn't been written to, up to 50 at a time, and lines them up in Ready to send.

features.name: Watch this area
features.text: Watch this area turns building permits and certificates of occupancy from the last 45 days into leads on Needs you, strongest RF need first, with the state's law. A lead with an email gets a first email in Ready to send, unsent.

features.name: Make a job
features.text: + Job on a Prospects row, or Make a job on a lead, puts the building on the board as a Lead with address, pin, building, permit, RF need, size and contact filled in. Not for us drops a lead.

features.name: Call list
features.text: Call list (CSV) downloads the rows shown, with each building's trigger and how far away a neighbour's permit sits.

features.name: Pitch deck
features.text: Pitch is a deck a DAS firm shows a building owner: why coverage, value beyond code, how a job runs, what we need, what you get, the tools, choosing an integrator and who else does this work, from 103 cited sources.

features.name: Pitch for a building
features.text: Pick a job for a slide on that building's systems and link budget, and where no rule requires a system the deck says why to choose one. Your firm's details go on every slide; it prints one slide per page.

features.name: DAS course
features.text: DAS has a DAS course link for accounts given the course, opening it in its own tab. Progress saves to your sign-in and merges, so a phone and a PC stay in step. Cody's login opens his own edition; every other login opens the team edition, written for anyone coming from another RF trade. Its Back button goes back a page in the course, and from the course's first page back to DAStastic.

areas.name: PIM
areas.summary: An app-wide passive intermodulation reference: limits, standards, checklists, procedures, connector torque and a PIM calculator, every row with its sources.

features.name: PIM calculator
features.text: Enter F1, F2, tone power and measured PIM: it lists the IM3, IM5, IM7 and IM9 products both ways to 3 decimals, flags any landing in 12 uplink bands, and gives the result in dBc. DAStastic lite has it under DAS.

features.name: Acceptance limits
features.text: Twenty limits with their condition and who uses them: -140 dBc (-97 dBm) as the legacy system pass, -150 dBc as the receiver-sensitivity target, -153 dBc as the common part spec, and DAS segment limits.

features.name: Requirements and standards
features.text: Forty-nine rows of PIM requirements by topic, item, value, spec, section and note, each linked to its source.

features.name: PIM checklists
features.text: Eight lists from pre-test planning and on-site safety to fault finding, connector care, close-out and DAS PIM, each with All / None, a done count and folding, ticked in this browser.

features.name: PIM procedures
features.text: Six step-by-step procedures, each with a Pass line where the research gives one: residual PIM check, static test, dynamic tap test, distance-to-PIM, connector inspection and cleaning, and the DAS passive network test.

features.name: Connector torque
features.text: Torque, tool and note for 9 connector types, with every value where sources differ. ANDREW's 2025 jumper bulletin (7617394 Rev H) sits beside the makers' figures, NEX10 4 to 5 N·m against 1.5: use the maker of the connector on your cable.

features.name: Causes, analysers and reports
features.text: What causes PIM and the fix (21), PIM analysers by vendor (13), PIM in a DAS (22), what a PIM report holds (23), a 39-term glossary and the 54-source list, every row linked.

areas.name: Parts
areas.summary: An app-wide reference for RF cables, connectors, components and suppliers from makers' datasheets, with a cable loss calculator and building-material wall loss.

features.name: Cable loss calculator
features.text: Pick one of 25 cables, a frequency (800 MHz default) and a run (200 ft) for total dB and dB per 100 ft, interpolated between datasheet points. The same calculator sits on a job's Materials step.

features.name: Stop bands in the calculator
features.text: A frequency inside a radiating cable's stop band, such as RLKU's 650 to 750, 1330 to 1430 and 2025 to 2100 MHz, gives no loss figure and says the cable doesn't carry it.

features.name: Find a supplier
features.text: 35 suppliers, filtered by name, product or note and by makers or distributors, with what each makes or sells, public-safety notes and sources.

features.name: Cable table
features.text: 26 cables with family, outer diameter, bend radius, loss per 100 ft at 150, 450, 700, 850, 1900 and 2600 MHz, rating, use, maker and part examples.

features.name: Connector table
features.text: N, 7/16 DIN, 4.3-10, NEX10, QMA, SMA, TNC, BNC and F with impedance, top frequency, low-PIM rating, torque, interface standard, use and notes.

features.name: Component types
features.text: 21 component types, from couplers, splitters and hybrids to BDAs, fiber DAS, battery backup, 2-hour pathways and annunciators, with what to pick by, ratings, makers and part examples.

features.name: Material rules and checklists
features.text: 22 DAS and ERCES material rules with their code references, and 5 selection checklists (feeder cable, connectors, splitter or coupler, ERCES compliance, BOM review) ticked in this browser.

features.name: Wall loss calculator
features.text: Pick a material from ITU-R P.2040 (concrete by default), a frequency and a thickness: it gives the loss through one slab with its permittivity and conductivity, the 3GPP TR 38.901 figure and up to 4 measured values nearby.

features.name: Building material tables
features.text: 15 typical wall assemblies, 139 measured losses by material, 51 P.2040 parameter rows and 11 TR 38.901 formulas, each row with its source.

areas.name: Data & updates
areas.summary: Where DAStastic downloads and keeps its data and holds the keys, and where the admin manages logins, the DAS course, server files and Push to ATAK.

features.name: Needs you here
features.text: Data & updates opens with what needs the admin: a source that's on with no key, a source whose last run failed, and WiGLE areas waiting a day or more for Cody's PC. When nothing does, it says so.

features.name: WiGLE through Cody's PC
features.text: WiGLE refuses the server's address, so a WiGLE request waits in a queue and Cody's PC fetches it every 15 minutes while it's on; the points stay on the server. The WiGLE key shows Saved · via Cody's PC, with how many areas wait and when the PC last brought points, and a key a source refuses shows Saved, refused.

features.name: Automatic updates
features.text: One switch downloads each selected source when its interval has passed and its source file has changed. It checks every 10 minutes, runs up to 4 sources at once, and starts switched off. A failed download tries again after 2 hours.

features.name: Update over which network
features.text: Update over sets the links updates use: All, Wi-Fi, Ethernet, or cellular and phone tether. Wi-Fi and Ethernet are the default, and a line says which link this copy is on and whether updates run on it.

features.name: Connection check
features.text: The Connection panel shows online or offline, the link and adapter, milliseconds to the FCC, the last check and what the browser reports. It rechecks every 15 seconds while offline and every 2 minutes online; Check now asks at once.

features.name: Update all
features.text: Update all runs every source at once, selected or not, and downloads only what is newer; sources with no key saved are skipped and named. On the server the button reads Pull everything to the server.

features.name: State limits
features.text: Limit FCC data to a list of states, or leave it blank for the whole US. Carrier coverage states set which states the FCC Broadband Map loads, about 100 MB to 2 GB of download each.

features.name: Data sources list
features.text: Each downloaded source has a switch, what it gives, its key, cost and terms, how often it runs (6 hours to monthly), Run now, its last result, its data's age in green, amber or red, the next check and rows.

features.name: Why a source isn't downloading
features.text: Each source says in one line what stops it: switched off, no key, last try failed, no mission area, offline, a skipped link, automatic updates off, or not in this build. A load a restart cut short says so, with its last step.

features.name: Download progress
features.text: A running source shows its current step in its status line, including each stage of an FCC licence rebuild.

features.name: Switched-off sources keep their data
features.text: Switching an FCC licence source off stops its checks and downloads but keeps what it loaded: the next licence rebuild reuses its saved file.

features.name: DAS marks
features.text: A DAS tag marks each source, key and setting the DAS tab reads, with a line saying what the DAS tab takes from it.

features.name: Used live and researched sources
features.text: Used live as you work lists the maps, terrain, address search, building outlines, radar and live ships DAStastic reads as you go. Other open and crowd sources lists the researched ones it doesn't use, with key, cost, terms and why.

features.name: Your API keys
features.text: One row each for WiGLE, OpenCelliD, aisstream, Mouser, Digi-Key, Shippo and the FCC Broadband Map: saved or not, what it unlocks, Get a key, the last fetch, and Remove on a second press. A typed key never shows again.

features.name: Crowd data for the pin
features.text: One press fetches WiGLE, OpenCelliD, LoRaWAN gateways, SatNOGS stations, WSPR or PSKReporter for the pin and radius; an area fetched recently isn't downloaded again. WiGLE and OpenCelliD need their keys, and WiGLE and WSPR run in the personal build only.

features.name: Import your own layer
features.text: A CSV, KML, KMZ, GeoJSON or GPX file becomes a named map layer, with a count of its points; importing again under the same name replaces it.

features.name: Import labels
features.text: A RadioReference-style CSV (frequency, licence, tone, alpha tag, description, mode, tag) merges into your labels, keeping what is already there where the file is blank.

features.name: Crowd and imported layers
features.text: Lists every crowd source and imported layer on this copy with its point count and when it was last fetched.

features.name: Look up an FCC ID
features.text: An FCC ID or grantee code gives the maker and its grants: grantee, date and purpose, plus bands, booster class and power for DAS and booster makers. When the FCC refuses DAStastic, the grants kept here show.

features.name: Maker list
features.text: Maker names come from the FCC's own current grantee list, which the DAStastic site hands to every copy, or the FCC's 2021 open data when the site can't be reached. One person imports the FCC's download; the web version hides the import.

features.name: Import FCC grant searches
features.text: Files saved from the FCC's Authorization Search import as grants with their bands; saying the search was by booster class and power fills those in. The DAS pre-survey's booster list reads them.

features.name: Ways in
features.text: Every way to reach DAStastic or its data, from the server and Cody's PC to field packs, exports and Push to ATAK, with each one's version and which work with Cody's PC off. On a phone each way is a card.

features.name: People and logins
features.text: The admin adds a person with a role (view, full, admin or AHJ reviewer) and gets their password, shown once; changes a role, resets a password, or removes someone on a second press. Each row shows when they were last here.

features.name: Temporary logins
features.text: A login can have a last day, for an inspector or someone watching a test: it works through that day, then can't sign in and its open sessions stop. The people list shows until or ended, and End now ends one today. A new password keeps the last day; the last admin can't be ended.

features.name: Your account
features.text: Anyone signed in presses their name in the header for Your account: change their own password (the current one first, then at least 10 characters) or sign out. A change signs out their other devices and keeps this one signed in; wrong current passwords count toward the same lock as signing in. An AHJ reviewer has the same from the review page. A forgotten password: Cody makes a new one in People and logins, and the sign-in page says so.

features.name: Sign in with Google
features.text: The sign-in page has Sign in with Google beside the password. A Google account signs in only as the login the admin linked it to (People and logins, Google…), and only while that login hasn't ended; passwords keep working. Data & updates and the people list show each person's first Google sign-in. Not in DAStastic for Android, whose web view Google refuses: there the password signs in.

features.name: Who has the DAS course
features.text: Tick an account to give it the DAS course, and see each one's lessons done, mastery, exams passed, current lesson and last use. Admins start ticked and can be unticked, AHJ reviewer logins can't have it, and unticking keeps progress.

features.name: Server files
features.text: The admin sees what the server keeps (DAS job files, notes, field packs, backups and app data) with sizes, dates and free disk, and downloads a copy of any file. Nothing here changes a file; logins, keys and the sign-in secret never show.

features.name: Push to ATAK settings
features.text: Network multicast on or off, the multicast group (blank means 239.2.3.1:6969) and an optional TAK Server host and port over plain TCP. Each address is checked as a host and port when saved.

features.name: Admin only
features.text: Team logins never see Data & updates: on the server it says the tab is for the admin login, and the Push to ATAK button is hidden for them too.

areas.name: Help
areas.summary: The built-in guide: how each tab works, the keys, where the data comes from, which build this is and how to install the Android app.

features.name: Help window
features.text: The ? button in the header, or the ? or F1 key, opens Help at the section for the tab you're on; F1 works while typing. Esc or a click outside closes it.

features.name: Search and jump
features.text: A search box narrows Help to the sections that mention what you type, and a chip for each section jumps straight to it.

features.name: 27 sections
features.text: Quick start, Searching, Filters, Map, Area report, Analyzer, Dashboard, Topology, Site profile, Agencies, Spectrum, Mission, Search, Cell sites, Find a signal, Replay, Compare, Receivers, Data & updates, Notes, keys, walls, sources, credits, glossary, Android and files. DAS, PIM, Parts and Start have none.

features.name: Quick start
features.text: Points a first-time user to the Start tab, then walks through picking a place, searching, narrowing with the filter rail, reading the Area report and making a mission.

features.name: What's new
features.text: A link at the top of Help opens the release notes: History, every release oldest first with its own time (Newest first turns it round), then Current build, what DAStastic does now area by area, with the build this copy runs. One search covers both.

features.name: Data credits and this build
features.text: Says whether this copy is the personal or the sold build, lists what the sold build leaves out and why, and carries the FCC, OpenCelliD, OpenStreetMap and Overture notices.

features.name: Mouse and keyboard
features.text: A table of the app-wide keys: ? or F1, N for a note, Ctrl+K for Search, L and / for the filter rail and its row keys, the Pin box, spectrum and topology zoom, Analyzer, DAS floors and walk-test undo.

features.name: Walls on floor plans
features.text: Explains the DAS floor-plan wall tools step by step: draw with snap, snip, lasso, Smart materials, review colours, remove, undo and redo, the best-tool button and every key.

features.name: Where the data comes from
features.text: Lists each data source in plain words, which ones the personal build alone carries, what isn't in any public list (federal users, cellular sites by site), and which predictions are free space or terrain.

features.name: Android app download
features.text: Help › Android app downloads DAStastic for Android 1.2 without signing in, and walks through installing it outside the Play Store, reading the phone in the walk test and correcting it against a calibrated instrument.

features.name: Where your files are
features.text: Says where each copy keeps things: the server keeps its data, jobs, packs and notes; Cody's PC keeps FCC data locally and docs, packs, backups and notes in Drive; the web version and lite keep everything in the browser.

features.name: Help links in the app
features.text: Links elsewhere in DAStastic, such as Ways in's Android row, open Help at the matching section.

areas.name: Across every tab
areas.summary: What works the same on every tab: the filter rail, exports, links, keys, looks, notes, the drop spot, address boxes, downloads and the header.

features.name: Filter rail
features.text: Beside the content, one rail filters every tab that shows results: Sources in three groups (licensed and registered, crowd and networks, mine), Signal type, Band, Carrier, Agency, Category and Station type, each with counts and an all or none box.

features.name: Rail fits the screen
features.text: From 1,100 px the rail docks left of the content, open from 1,600 px and folded below; L or a click opens it and the choice is kept. Narrower it opens over the content; on a phone it is a bottom sheet.

features.name: Only, and back again
features.text: Only shows one value and hides the rest; pressing it again puts back what was on. Alt+click does the same, and a box at the top finds a filter by name.

features.name: All / None on checklists
features.text: Every checklist has one All / None box (a dash when only some are ticked) and a count such as 3 of 12 done; long lists fold until opened and remember it.

features.name: Public safety, Cellular, Everything
features.text: A switch sets the rail for the work. Public safety leads with Band and Agency, public safety agencies picked; Cellular leads with Carrier, rows naming a carrier picked, towers and OpenCelliD on; Everything leads with Sources. Every section stays in all three.

features.name: Carrier filter
features.text: AT&T, Verizon, T-Mobile, FirstNet, UScellular and Dish / Boost, read from a tower's owner, a licensee or a cell ID, with one name per carrier everywhere: Cingular reads as AT&T.

features.name: Agency filter
features.text: One name per licensee by case and punctuation only, so FAIRFAX, COUNTY OF and Fairfax, County of are one agency. The 40 with most rows list first and the filter box finds the rest; Site profile's Top licensees bars filter on a click.

features.name: Unknown named by radio service
features.text: Licences with no mode on file read Trunked, mode not on file, or Microwave link from their FCC radio service where the service says so. The rest stay Unknown, counted.

features.name: Exports match the screen
features.text: Export in the rail gives CSV and KML that follow every filter (tick Everything the search found for all rows), the ATAK package, and Prep sheet, which prints the Site profile's frequency checklist.

features.name: Any table as CSV
features.text: Display settings download any table on the view as a CSV named by its heading.

features.name: Links carry the view
features.text: The address bar holds the tab, pin and radius or county, text, frequency, FCC fields, filters, the switch, Fixed sites only, the Analyzer expression and the heatmap, so a reload or a shared link opens the same view.

features.name: Keyboard shortcuts
features.text: Ctrl+K Search, N a note, ? or F1 Help, L the filter rail and / to find a filter, with arrows, Space, O (only), A (all on) and Esc inside it; Alt+← Back; [ ] steps DAS floors. Keys wait while you type.

features.name: Look and skins
features.text: The Look button sets the skin (Match system, Smoke, Haze, Dusk, Liquid, Daylight and nine colour skins), texture, light and shadow, accent, a backdrop photo, glass, Reduce transparency and Motion, saved in this browser. ◐ switches light and dark.

features.name: Back and Close
features.text: Back and Close sit beside the Look button, for DAStastic's own window, which has no browser buttons. Back steps between tabs; Close shuts the window or says to press Ctrl+W.

features.name: Note button
features.text: On every screen: a voice note, the screen recorded while you talk and point, a photo with voice or words, or just words, each tagged with the screen, pin and mission. The web version and DAStastic lite keep notes in the browser.

features.name: Share with Cody
features.text: Share with Cody, pressed twice, emails a note to Cody as a numbered DAStastic report with its files; each person's send code comes in their link. A team login's note on the server goes straight to Cody's copy.

features.name: Drop spot
features.text: Drop files, folders, zips or old emails anywhere on any tab, or press the Intake chip. Plain documents fill empty spots in the job's Files, readings and prices wait for a press, and anything unsure goes on Needs a look.

features.name: Undo and what's still needed
features.text: Nothing already there is written over, any filing can be undone item by item or the whole drop at once, and each drop ends with what the job still needs. Only logins that can make changes see Intake.

features.name: What the drop spot refuses
features.text: Anything that runs code stays out of a job's Files: web pages, SVGs, PDFs with JavaScript or a media player, Office macros, programs and shortcuts. A file whose name lies about its contents is held.

features.name: Stored files open walled off
features.text: A stored file that could hold a script, such as a web page or an SVG, opens walled off from the app, so it can't act as you. PDFs, pictures, video and audio open as usual.

features.name: Virus scan where there is one
features.text: Where ClamAV is on the machine, every dropped file is virus-scanned and a hit is refused. Without it, each result says it wasn't virus-scanned: the checks look at what a file is.

features.name: Address boxes fill in
features.text: A job's address, the firm's mailing address, Prospects' Where and Start's address bring up the full address as you type, nearest to where you're working first. Arrows move, Enter or a click takes it; towns and counties work with no signal.

features.name: House number and typos are enough
features.text: A house number and street, misspelled or not, find the address: the Census geocoder answers beside Photon, the typed number first, nearby states at once and every state after a pause. Enter or Tab finishes it when one address carries your number.

features.name: The box says what it's doing
features.text: An address box says when it's still looking, when it's looking in every state, and when the lookup isn't answering, in place of an empty list.

features.name: Stop all downloads
features.text: Stop all downloads in Data & updates stops every download at its next megabyte and starts nothing, automatic updates included, until Resume downloads. A file cut short never replaces the copy you had, and the stop holds through a restart.

features.name: Field packs
features.text: Data & updates makes a field pack for chosen states or around the pin, for the web version and DAStastic lite: licences, towers, broadcast, NOAA, FAA, 911 centres, microwave links and prospect buildings, never your work, keys or crowd layers.

features.name: Connection and mission chips
features.text: The header shows the connection (online, over Wi-Fi, Ethernet, cellular or VPN, Updating…, auto) and opens Data & updates; a signed-in login sees its name and Sign out. The mission chip names the active mission and opens Mission.

features.name: Phone layout
features.text: On a phone: one column, the header scrolls away, the tab bar sticks and scrolls sideways, the map comes first with its tools under it, and the filters open as a bottom sheet. Controls are at least 44 px.

areas.name: Integrations
areas.summary: How DAStastic connects to ATAK and TAK, to your own mailbox, to BDA alarms, to an Android phone's radio, to parts and shipping services, and to Cody's note mailer.

features.name: ATAK data package
features.text: ⇩ ATAK saves what's on screen as a TAK data package: a marker per site coloured by signal type, the pin and its ring, and the heatmap showing, nearest 3,000 sites first. DAStastic lite's Send to ATAK makes the same package.

features.name: Live push from the PC
features.text: 📡 Push to ATAK sends live markers to every ATAK, iTAK and WinTAK on the PC's networks over the TAK multicast, and to a TAK Server if set. Pushing again updates them; they fade a day after the last push.

features.name: Live push from the server
features.text: The server's admin login pushes the same live markers to a TAK Server set in Data & updates. Team logins get the button only in the Android app, which pushes from the phone.

features.name: Push in the web version
features.text: With no PC behind it, Push to ATAK hands the package to ATAK or iTAK through an iPhone's share sheet; on Android, where Chrome won't share a .zip, it saves the zip and a card gives the two steps to open it in ATAK; on a computer it saves the zip for ATAK or WinTAK.

features.name: TAK team on the map
features.text: The map's TAK team (this network) layer listens on the TAK multicast and shows ATAK, iTAK and WinTAK users by callsign, and their markers, stale ones grey. Nothing is kept on disk, and it stops when nobody's looking.

features.name: Live push from the Android app
features.text: In DAStastic for Android on Wi-Fi, 📡 Push to ATAK sends the same live markers from the phone over its Wi-Fi: to ATAK on the phone itself and to every ATAK, iTAK and WinTAK on that Wi-Fi, for team logins too, in the server and the web version alike. Off Wi-Fi it saves the package as before.

features.name: TAK team in the Android app
features.text: In DAStastic for Android, the TAK team (this network) layer listens on the Wi-Fi the phone is on for ATAK, iTAK and WinTAK users on other devices and shows them by callsign, with their markers, in the server and the web version alike. The phone's own ATAK doesn't show in it: on Cody's phone the layer heard nothing from it while ATAK sent its position every 30 seconds. Positions stay in memory; it stops when the layer is off, the app is in the background, or nobody has looked for two minutes.

features.name: DAStastic maps in ATAK
features.text: Download an ATAK, WinTAK or iTAK map source file for any built-in base map, or a map you imported by tile address, so ATAK shows the same ground as DAStastic.

features.name: Your own mailbox
features.text: Each signed-in person connects their own mailbox once with an app password: Gmail, Yahoo, iCloud, AOL, Zoho, Fastmail, GMX or any IMAP and SMTP host. DAStastic sends only on Send, from their address, with a copy in Sent.

features.name: Microsoft and web mail
features.text: Outlook.com and Microsoft 365 aren't connected: they need Microsoft's own sign-in, which DAStastic doesn't have. The web version and lite keep Open in my mail, which opens your own mail app.

features.name: Tagged replies
features.text: Every email DAStastic sends carries an [RFR …] tag. Every 5 minutes it reads only tagged mail, files each reply on its quote, prospect or job, marks an opt-out Do not contact, and holds a reply from an unknown address. Their attachments are checked as a drop is; a refused one waits in the drop spot with its reason.

features.name: Who a reply vouches for
features.text: A saved contact on a free mail service (Gmail, Outlook and the like) vouches only for that address, not for everyone on the service.

features.name: Mail sign-in help
features.text: A pasted address with invisible characters is cleaned, an app password copied with spaces works, and when the provider refuses, its own reason shows with what to fix.

features.name: BDA alarms by SNMP
features.text: A job's Overview › Monitoring takes SNMP v1 and v2c traps from any maker's BDA, files each on its job by source address or community, and names the NFPA 1225 18.14 signal. A BDA silent 24 hours reads not heard from.

features.name: Monitoring switch
features.text: Monitoring listens on no port until the admin switches it on, then on UDP 1162 by default. On the server, the firewall has to let that port in from the buildings for any trap to arrive.

features.name: SNMPv3 alarms
features.text: A BDA added as v3 takes its user, SHA-1, SHA-2 or MD5 authentication and AES-128 privacy. Its passphrases go to the sealed key file and never show again; a trap files only when its key checks out, and a replayed one is refused.

features.name: BDA alarms to the owner
features.text: While monitoring is on, a job with an open alarm or a quiet BDA gets an email to the owner lined up in Ready to send, sent only on a click.

features.name: Phone radio in walk tests
features.text: DAStastic for Android gives the page the phone's serving and neighbour LTE and 5G cells: carrier, band, PCI, RSRP, RSRQ and SINR. The DAS walk test's Read the phone and Start walk use them; they never count toward a public-safety pass.

features.name: Note mailer
features.text: Send email now posts a note to a Google Apps Script mailer under Cody's account. It checks the sender's code, numbers the report per person, adds a short topic, and emails Cody from a no-reply address with files up to 20 MB.

areas.name: Data sources
areas.summary: Every source DAStastic downloads or reads live: what it gives, how often it refreshes, whether it needs a key, and which build carries it.

features.name: FCC ULS licences
features.text: Private and commercial land mobile, broadcast auxiliary, paging, and marine and aviation ground licences, rebuilt into one search table. Weekly, on by default, downloading only files the FCC changed; no key, every build.

features.name: FCC licensee contacts
features.text: Each licence's own contact (name, phone, email, mailing address), kept with every licence import, so DAS consent letters go to the licence's contact. No key, every build.

features.name: FCC cellular 800 MHz sites
features.text: Each carrier's licensed 800 MHz cellular sites: where, which tower, frequencies each way, power and antenna height, about 22,700 sites (24 MB). Weekly, on by default, no key, every build.

features.name: FCC carrier spectrum
features.text: Which carrier holds which block in each market: cellular, PCS, AWS, 600 and 700 MHz, 3.45 GHz, C-band and CBRS, from the FCC's market licences (about 115 MB). Weekly, on by default, no key.

features.name: FCC microwave links
features.text: Licensed point-to-point microwave paths, placed at both ends for the Microwave backhaul layer. Weekly when switched on; off by default (about 210 MB); no key.

features.name: Pending microwave links
features.text: Microwave links filed with the FCC but not yet granted, drawn dashed on the backhaul layer with filing number, purpose and date. Weekly when on; off by default, a 445 MB download.

features.name: FCC towers
features.text: Registered antenna structures and their heights, linked to licence sites. Weekly, on by default, no key, every build.

features.name: Broadcast stations
features.text: AM, FM, TV, low-power and translator stations from the FCC Media Bureau. Weekly, on by default, no key; saved lists stand in when the FCC refuses the download.

features.name: NOAA Weather Radio
features.text: About 1,000 NOAA Weather Radio transmitters and the counties each one warns. Weekly, on by default, no key, every build.

features.name: FAA aviation frequencies
features.text: Towers, ATIS, approach, CTAF, navaids and ILS from the FAA's 28-day NASR cycle. Checked weekly, on by default, no key, every build.

features.name: 911 call centres
features.text: About 8,600 call centres from the FCC's PSAP registry, placed at town level; the FCC last updated the rows in 2017. Monthly, on by default, no key.

features.name: Satellite earth stations
features.text: About 470 protected C-band receive sites, 3.6 to 4.2 GHz, with where each dish points, its gain and height. Weekly, on by default, no key.

features.name: FCC equipment makers
features.text: Every grantee code that starts an FCC ID, with its company, from the FCC's own list on the DAStastic site (2021 open data if the site can't be reached). Every 90 days, on by default, no key.

features.name: FCC equipment grants
features.text: Grants looked up live, one FCC ID at a time, plus the DAS and booster makers' grants with their bands imported from FCC searches and passed to every copy in the site's grantee file.

features.name: FCC carrier coverage
features.text: Each carrier's modelled 3G, 4G and 5G coverage and signal for the carrier-coverage states, from the FCC Broadband Map. Checked monthly, off by default, needs a free FCC login; a big load stops above 8 GB free disk.

features.name: FCC broadband extras
features.text: Resolved coverage challenges, verifications and audits, fixed wireless offered, and carriers' filed link budgets: about 2.5 GB a release, 1 GB kept. Monthly, off by default, same FCC login.

features.name: OpenCelliD for mission areas
features.text: Cell towers around each mission area, asked in 1.9 km tiles. Every 2 weeks when on, off by default; needs your OpenCelliD key (1,000 requests a day, CC BY-SA 4.0). Every build.

features.name: OpenCelliD every US cell
features.text: Every cell OpenCelliD has in the US from its country files (MCC 310 to 316), with first and last seen and PCI or PSC. Off until switched on: a large download, then monthly; needs your key.

features.name: WiGLE sightings
features.text: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and cell sightings in each mission area. Weekly when on, off by default; needs your WiGLE name and token. Personal build only: WiGLE's terms are non-commercial. On the server, which WiGLE refuses, a request waits in a queue that Cody's PC fetches (every 15 minutes while it's on) and sends back; the points stay on the server.

features.name: RepeaterBook repeaters
features.text: Amateur and GMRS repeaters, listed every 2 weeks but off: Your API keys doesn't take its token, because RepeaterBook's policy discourages tools that mix sources. Personal build only.

features.name: LoRaWAN gateways (TTN)
features.text: The Things Network gateways near each mission area. Weekly, on by default, no key, every build; an area fetched in the last 7 days is skipped.

features.name: Helium hotspots
features.text: Active Helium IoT hotspots for each mission area, at positions Helium blurs. Weekly, no key, off by default: each pass reads the whole network, about 190 MB.

features.name: Meshtastic mesh radios
features.text: Mesh radios that share their position (meshmap.net, one 4 MB file), with their region's channel frequency, for each mission area. Daily, on by default, no key, every build.

features.name: SatNOGS ground stations
features.text: Satellite ground stations and their antennas, kept to the area. Monthly, on by default, no key (CC BY-SA 4.0), every build.

features.name: WSPR stations
features.text: Stations heard or transmitting in the area in the last 24 hours, from wspr.live. Daily, no key. Personal build only: wspr.live is non-commercial.

features.name: PSKReporter monitors
features.text: Digital-mode monitors and the stations they heard in the area in the last hour. Daily, on by default, no key, every build.

features.name: Signal ID Wiki catalog
features.text: About 600 signals with modes and bandwidths, for what a signal could be; fetched on first start, then monthly. Personal build only: the wiki grants no licence to reuse its content.

features.name: Artemis signal library
features.text: A waterfall picture and audio clip for each Signal ID Wiki signal, from Artemis's GitHub home (Artemis-Database), about 300 MB. Checked monthly, downloaded only when a later release is out; off by default. Personal build only.

features.name: Live ships (aisstream)
features.text: Live AIS ships for the map's box while the Ships layer is on, stopping 3 minutes after the last look; ships unheard for 30 minutes drop off. Needs your aisstream key. Personal build only.

features.name: Maps kept for mission areas
features.text: The four USGS base maps to zoom 16 (shaded relief to 13) and terrain for each mission area, about 1.3 GB an area. Monthly when on, off by default; kept tiles aren't fetched again.

features.name: DAS prospect lists
features.text: NCES public and private schools, IPEDS colleges, CMS hospitals and nursing homes, Overture places (malls, arenas, hotels and more), and high-rises around mission areas. Monthly, on by default, no key.

features.name: Building permits and occupancy
features.text: Permits for buildings going up, additions and major alterations, and certificates of occupancy, from city and county open data for the states set. Weekly, on by default; 24 of 52 datasets start on, each with its own switch.

features.name: Fire department registry
features.text: 27,117 fire departments and 8,092 stations from the USFA registry, for a DAS job's AHJ guess. Monthly, on by default, no key; the registry stopped updating in June 2026 and says so.

features.name: DAS part prices
features.text: Each supplier's price list re-read from its link, and open requests for quote repriced with your Mouser and Digi-Key keys. Weekly, on by default.

features.name: Base maps and overlays
features.text: OpenStreetMap street and Esri hi-res satellite, read live and never kept; USGS imagery, topo and relief and Census county lines, kept as viewed; NEXRAD radar from Iowa State, live every 5 minutes. No keys.

features.name: Terrain tiles
features.text: Elevation tiles from Terrain Tiles on AWS for terrain profiles, coverage estimates and donor paths, kept once fetched. No key.

features.name: Address search
features.text: Photon (OpenStreetMap data) answers address boxes. On the server and PC a street address goes to the US Census Bureau's geocoder at the same time, and a pause with nothing nearby asks every state. No key.

features.name: Building outlines and tunnels
features.text: OpenStreetMap building outlines and road and rail tunnels, asked of three Overpass servers at once per DAS job; tunnel answers are kept 30 days. No key.

features.name: Overture buildings
features.text: Building outlines and estimated heights from Overture Maps extracts made ahead for the mission areas, used where OpenStreetMap has none. No key; reports carry the ODbL notice.

features.name: National Structure Inventory
features.text: One building's occupancy, stories, square feet, basement, year built, height and people by day and night from USACE, asked live per DAS job and shown as estimates. No key.

features.name: RadioID.net look-ups
features.text: Who a DMR or NXDN radio ID belongs to: call sign, name, city, state and country, asked one ID at a time when someone asks and kept 30 days. No key, every build.

features.name: Researched, not added
features.text: RadioReference (needs Premium and a paid licence), OpenSky, aprs.fi, beaconDB, KiwiSDR and WebSDR lists, and CellMapper stay out; Reverse Beacon Network and Ookla open data could be added. Data & updates says why for each.

areas.name: Versions and where it runs
areas.summary: Each copy of DAStastic, who gets in and what it carries: the 24/7 server, Cody's PC, the web version, DAStastic lite, the Android app and the install kits.

features.name: 24/7 server
features.text: The main DAStastic runs around the clock on AWS at its own web address, for invited logins. It holds the whole-US FCC data, carrier coverage, crowd data for the mission areas, and the team's DAS jobs and notes.

features.name: Logins and roles
features.text: Each person signs in with their own login. View looks, searches and leaves notes; Full also works DAS jobs, missions and notes; Admin also has keys, updates and people; an AHJ reviewer sees only the jobs shared with it.

features.name: Passwords and sessions
features.text: DAStastic makes each password and shows it once. A sign-in lasts 14 days; a password reset or removal ends that person's sessions at once, and a signed-out page goes straight to the sign-in page.

features.name: Sign-in lockout
features.text: Eight wrong passwords for one name within 15 minutes lock that name for 15 minutes. The last admin login can't be removed or demoted.

features.name: Per-login build
features.text: On the server the admin login gets the personal build with every source; every other login gets the sold build. The server holds the keys it uses, and the app never shows a key.

features.name: Installable app
features.text: The server's page installs as an app from Chrome or Edge's address bar on a PC, or Add to Home Screen on a phone. It keeps nothing offline: every answer comes fresh from the server.

features.name: Cody's PC app
features.text: A second full copy runs in its own window on Cody's PC as the personal build and starts with Windows. It keeps its own FCC data and DAS jobs for work with no signal; the PC and the server don't sync.

features.name: Opened from the folder
features.text: Opening DAStastic's page straight from its folder goes to the running app, or says how to start it.

features.name: Remote link from the PC
features.text: Remote access on Cody's PC turns a Tailscale link to the PC copy on or off. People sign in with the same roles, and the link works only while the PC and DAStastic run; Ways in shows it on the PC only.

features.name: Full web version
features.text: The full app runs in any browser from GitHub Pages, always as the sold build. The FCC data for the pin's state loads by itself, the PC's own engine runs in the browser, and each person's work stays in that browser.

features.name: Not in the web version
features.text: Carrier coverage, live ships, Artemis, the TAK team layer, live push to ATAK, mailbox mail, building facts from NSI, Find high-rises, prospect list downloads, updates, the kit and logins run on the server or PC only.

features.name: Packs tab
features.text: In the web version, Data & updates becomes Packs: the pack in use, a pack file or a state from the site, the packs kept in this browser, then the key, crowd data, import and FCC ID panels.

features.name: Web version with no signal
features.text: Opened once with signal, the web version keeps its page, its code and the 16.5 MB engine, so a DAS job can be made and saved with no signal. With Data Saver on it waits until asked.

features.name: DAStastic lite
features.text: The phone app keeps one area's data on the phone: Map, List, Report, Log with Find a signal, DAS grid tests, read-only prospects, the PIM calculator and code numbers, and Packs, plus Send to ATAK and the Note button.

features.name: Lite with no signal
features.text: Lite's app files stay on the phone, packs stay in browser storage, USGS tiles are kept as viewed, and Save the map around the pin keeps USGS zoom 8 to 15, up to 6,000 tiles.

features.name: DAStastic for Android
features.text: Version 1.2, for Android 10 and up, opens the server full-screen and keeps the sign-in. Back on the first page offers the server, the web version, reload or exit, and downloads land in Downloads/DAStastic.

features.name: Android with no connection
features.text: When the server or the web version can't be reached, the app shows why, with Try again and a switch to the other one.

features.name: Code install kit
features.text: One zip someone unzips on a Windows PC and starts: the app with its own Python 3.12.10, and no data, keys or logins. Its welcome screen picks states and downloads the FCC data; it runs the sold build on a free port.

features.name: Full-copy install kit
features.text: A second kit carries the whole-US FCC data, carrier coverage, and the maps and terrain kept for no signal, so it opens with nothing to download. It leaves out keys, logins, anyone's own work, crowd data, the Signal ID Wiki and Artemis.

features.name: Kit updates
features.text: A kit copy checks the DAStastic site for a later kit at most hourly, shows an Update available chip with the notes, installs the zip picked under This copy of DAStastic and restarts. Data, jobs and settings stay.

features.name: Sold and personal builds
features.text: The sold build (team logins, the install kits, the web version and lite) leaves out WiGLE, RepeaterBook, wspr.live, the Signal ID Wiki, Artemis and live ships, whose terms bar selling or sharing. The personal build is the owner's alone.

features.name: Backups of your work
features.text: Every 6 hours a copy backs up your own work (missions, captures, labels, settings, notes, DAS jobs and course progress), never API keys or FCC data, and keeps the 14 newest. Cody's PC backs up to Drive.

features.name: Keys sealed
features.text: API keys, mailbox passwords and SNMPv3 passphrases sit outside every database file: sealed to the Windows account on a PC, and on the server in a key file only DAStastic's own user can read. No kit, backup or field pack carries them.

features.name: Heavy jobs at night
features.text: On the server, FCC licence rebuilds, carrier coverage, the broadband extras, pending microwave links and mission-area map tiles start only between 2 and 5 AM Eastern. Run now still starts at once.

features.name: Saves during a refresh
features.text: When a save meets an FCC refresh writing the database, DAStastic says nothing was changed and to try again in a few minutes.
